title.zh: 卷103 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車
title.en: Volume 103: Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai, Duanliu Liujuan, Gaoche
title.raw: 卷103 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車 Volume 103: Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai, Duanliu Liujuan, Gaoche

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車

translations.literal: Rouran; Xiongnu Yuwen Mohuai; Tuohe Duan Jiu Liujuan; Gaoche
translations.idiomatic: Rouran; Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu; Duan Jiu Liujuan of the Tuohe; Gaoche

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕，東胡之苗裔也，姓郁久閭氏。

translations.literal: The Rouran were descendants of the Eastern Hu, with the surname Yujiulü.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were a branch of the Eastern Hu and bore the clan name Yujiulü.

sentences.zh: 始神元之末，掠騎有得一奴，髮始齊眉，忘本姓名，其主字之曰木骨閭。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shenyuan era, raiding horsemen captured a slave whose hair had just grown to his eyebrows; he forgot his original name, and his master gave him the courtesy name Mugulü.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shenyuan reign, a raiding party took a slave whose hair had only reached his brows; he no longer remembered his birth name, and his master styled him Mugulü.

sentences.zh: 「木骨閭」者，首禿也。

translations.literal: "Mugulü" means "bald-headed."
translations.idiomatic: The name Mugulü means "bald head."

sentences.zh: 木骨閭與郁久閭聲相近，故後子孫因以為氏。

translations.literal: Mugulü and Yujiulü sound alike, so later descendants took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mugulü sounded close to Yujiulü, later generations adopted the latter as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 木骨閭既壯，免奴為騎卒。

translations.literal: When Mugulü came of age, he was freed from slavery and made a cavalry soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mugulü had grown to manhood, he was manumitted and enrolled as a mounted trooper.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，坐後期當斬，亡匿廣漠谿谷間，收合逋逃得百餘人，依紇突隣部。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mu, he was sentenced to execution for arriving late; he fled and hid in ravines of the vast desert, gathered fugitives numbering more than a hundred, and attached himself to the Hetulin tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu he was condemned to death for tardiness, fled into the gullies of the great desert, rallied more than a hundred runaways, and took refuge with the Hetulin clan.

sentences.zh: [2]木骨閭死，子車鹿會雄健，始有部眾，自號柔然，而役屬於國。

translations.literal: [2] When Mugulü died, his son Cheluhui, a man of martial prowess, first gathered a tribal following, styled himself Rouran, and became subject to the state.
translations.idiomatic: [2] After Mugulü's death his son Cheluhui, a formidable warrior, first mustered a following, took the title Rouran, and submitted to service under the Wei state.

sentences.zh: 後世祖以其無知，狀類於蟲，故改其號為蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shizu, because they were ignorant and resembled worms in appearance, changed their designation to Ruru.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taiwu, deeming them dull and wormlike in their ways, renamed them Ruru ("wriggling worms").

translations.literal: [Editorial note 3: The transmitted texts vary between 蟲 and 蠱 in the passage stating that Emperor Taiwu renamed them 蠕蠕 because they resembled worms.]
translations.idiomatic: [Scholarly note 3: Manuscripts disagree on whether the text reads 蟲 or 蠱 in the account of Taiwu's insulting rename 蠕蠕 ("wriggling worms"), distinct from their own name 柔然 (Rouran).]

sentences.zh: 車鹿會既為部帥，歲貢馬畜、貂豽皮，冬則徙度漠南，夏則還居漠北。

translations.literal: Once Cheluhui became tribal chief, he paid annual tribute of horses, livestock, and sable and badger pelts; in winter he moved south across the desert, and in summer returned to dwell north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheluhui became chief, his people sent yearly tribute of horses, herds, and furs; they wintered south of the Gobi and summered north of it.

sentences.zh: 車鹿會死，子吐奴傀立。

translations.literal: Cheluhui died, and his son Tunugui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheluhui died, his son Tunugui took his place.

sentences.zh: 吐奴傀死，子跋提立。

translations.literal: Tunugui died, and his son Bati succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tunugui was succeeded by his son Bati.

sentences.zh: 跋提死，子地粟袁立。

translations.literal: Bati died, and his son Disuyuan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Bati died and was followed by his son Disuyuan.

sentences.zh: 地粟袁死，其部分為二，地粟袁長子匹候跋繼父居東邊，次子縕紇提別居西邊。

translations.literal: When Disuyuan died, his tribe split in two: the eldest son Pihouba inherited his father's eastern seat, while the second son Wennihedi settled separately in the west.
translations.idiomatic: After Disuyuan's death the tribe divided: his eldest son Pihouba held the eastern lands his father had ruled, and his younger son Wennihedi established himself in the west.

sentences.zh: 及昭成崩，縕紇提附衞辰而貳於我。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng died, Wennihedi attached himself to Weichen and turned against us.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaocheng's death, Wennihedi allied with Weichen and rebelled against Wei.

sentences.zh: 登國中討之，蠕蠕移部遁走，追之，及於大磧南牀山下，大破之，虜其半部。

translations.literal: In the Dengguo era we campaigned against them; the Rouran moved their tribes and fled. Pursuing them, we caught them south of the great desert at Mount Chuang and inflicted a great defeat, capturing half the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengguo reign we marched against them; the Rouran shifted camp and fled, but our pursuit overtook them south of the great desert at Mount Chuang, where we routed them and took half the tribe captive.

sentences.zh: 匹候跋及部帥屋擊各收餘落遁走，遣長孫嵩及長孫肥追之，渡磧。

translations.literal: Pihouba and the tribal chief Wuji each gathered the remnants and fled. We sent Changsun Song and Changsun Fei in pursuit across the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Pihouba and the chief Wuji rallied the survivors and escaped; Changsun Song and Changsun Fei were dispatched in pursuit across the desert.

sentences.zh: 嵩至平望川，大破屋擊，禽之，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Song reached Pingwang River, routed Wuji decisively, captured him, and executed him as a public example.
translations.idiomatic: Song reached the Pingwang River, crushed Wuji's force, took him prisoner, and beheaded him before the army.

sentences.zh: 肥至涿邪山，及匹候跋，跋舉落請降。

translations.literal: Fei reached Zhuoye Mountain, overtook Pihouba, and Pihouba led his entire tribe in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fei came to Zhuoye Mountain, caught Pihouba, and Pihouba brought his whole following to submit.

sentences.zh: 獲縕紇提子曷多汗及曷多汗兄詰歸之、社崘、斛律等并宗黨數百人，分配諸部。

translations.literal: We captured Wennihedi's son Heduo Han and Heduo Han's elder brothers Jieguizhi, Shelun, Hulu, and several hundred clansmen, distributing them among the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Heduo Han, son of Wennihedi, was taken, together with his brothers Jieguizhi, Shelun, Hulu, and several hundred kinsmen, who were parcelled out among our tribes.

sentences.zh: 縕紇提西遁，將歸衞辰，太祖追之，至跋那山，縕紇提復降，太祖撫慰如舊。

translations.literal: Wennihedi fled west, intending to rejoin Weichen. The Taizu pursued him to Bana Mountain; Wennihedi submitted again, and the Taizu comforted him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wennihedi fled west toward Weichen, but Emperor Daowu pursued him to Bana Mountain, where he surrendered once more and was received with the same favor as before.

sentences.zh: 九年，曷多汗與社崘率部眾棄其父西走，長孫肥輕騎追之，至上郡跋那山，斬曷多汗，盡殪其眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Heduo Han and Shelun led their tribes west, abandoning their father. Changsun Fei with light cavalry pursued them to Bana Mountain in Shang Commandery, beheaded Heduo Han, and slaughtered his entire following.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Heduo Han and Shelun deserted their father and fled west with their people; Changsun Fei's light horse overtook them at Bana Mountain in Shang Commandery, killed Heduo Han, and annihilated his band.

sentences.zh: 社崘與數百人奔匹候跋，匹候跋處之南鄙，去其庭五百里，令其子四人監之。

translations.literal: Shelun fled with several hundred men to Pihouba. Pihouba settled them on his southern marches, five hundred li from his court, and set his four sons to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun reached Pihouba with a few hundred followers; Pihouba placed them on his southern frontier, five hundred li from his headquarters, under watch of his four sons.

sentences.zh: 既而社崘率其私屬執匹候跋四子而叛，襲匹候跋。

translations.literal: Before long Shelun led his personal retainers, seized Pihouba's four sons, rebelled, and attacked Pihouba.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shelun turned on his hosts: with his own men he seized Pihouba's four sons, rose in revolt, and struck at Pihouba.

sentences.zh: 諸子收餘眾，亡依高車斛律部。

translations.literal: The sons gathered the remnant forces and fled to take refuge with the Gaoche Hulu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The sons rallied what was left of their following and fled to the Gaoche under Hulu.

sentences.zh: 社崘兇狡有權變，月餘，乃釋匹候跋，歸其諸子，欲聚而殲之。

translations.literal: Shelun was fierce, cunning, and resourceful. After more than a month he released Pihouba and returned his sons, intending to gather them together and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun was brutal and full of stratagems; after a month he freed Pihouba and sent back his sons, planning to lure them in and wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 密舉兵襲匹候跋，殺匹候跋。

translations.literal: He secretly raised troops, attacked Pihouba by surprise, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck in secret and slew Pihouba.

sentences.zh: 子啟拔、吳頡等十五人歸于太祖。

translations.literal: His sons Qiba, Wu'er, and fifteen others came over to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen of Pihouba's kin, including Qiba and Wu'er, defected to Emperor Daowu.

sentences.zh: 社崘既殺匹候跋，懼王師討之，乃掠五原以西諸部，北度大漠。

translations.literal: After Shelun had killed Pihouba, fearing imperial punishment he raided the tribes west of Wuyuan and crossed the great desert to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shelun had killed Pihouba, he feared a punitive expedition, plundered the tribes west of Wuyuan, and fled north across the Gobi.

sentences.zh: 太祖以拔、頡為安遠將軍、平棘侯。

translations.literal: The Taizu appointed Ba and Er as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Marquis of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu made Ba and Er General Who Pacifies the Distance and Marquis of Pingji.

sentences.zh: [4]社崘與姚興和親。

translations.literal: [4] Shelun entered a marriage alliance with Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Shelun allied himself by marriage with Yao Xing of Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣材官將軍和突襲黜弗、素古延諸部，社崘遣騎救素古延，突逆擊破之。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent the Artisan-General He Tu to raid the Chufu and Suguyan tribes. Shelun dispatched cavalry to rescue Suguyan; Tu counterattacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu sent Artisan-General He Tu against the Chufu and Suguyan tribes; Shelun sent horsemen to relieve Suguyan, but Tu met them head-on and broke their force.

sentences.zh: 社崘遠遁漠北，侵高車，深入其地，遂并諸部，凶勢益振。

translations.literal: Shelun fled far into the northern desert, invaded the Gaoche, penetrated deep into their territory, and thereupon annexed the various tribes; his violent power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun withdrew deep into the northern steppe, invaded the Gaoche heartland, absorbed tribe after tribe, and his power swelled.

sentences.zh: 北徙弱洛水，始立軍法：千人為軍，軍置將一人，百人為幢，幢置帥一人；

translations.literal: He moved north to the Ruoluo River and first established military regulations: a thousand men formed an army, each army having one general; a hundred men formed a banner unit, each banner having one commander;
translations.idiomatic: Moving north to the Ruoluo River, he instituted military organization: units of a thousand men, each under a general; companies of a hundred, each under a commander;

sentences.zh: 先登者賜以虜獲，退懦者以石擊首殺之，或臨時捶撻。

translations.literal: those who charged first were rewarded with captives and booty; the cowardly who fell back were killed by stoning, or beaten on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: the first to scale the enemy were rewarded with plunder; cowards who hung back were stoned to death or flogged where they stood.

sentences.zh: 無文記，將帥以羊屎粗計兵數，後頗知刻木為記。

translations.literal: There were no written records; commanders roughly counted troops with sheep droppings, and later came partly to know how to keep tallies by carving wood.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing; commanders roughly tallied strength with sheep dung, and only later learned to keep count by notching wood.

sentences.zh: 其西北有匈奴餘種，國尤富強，部帥曰拔也稽，舉兵擊社崘，社崘逆戰於頞根河，大破之，後盡為社崘所并。

translations.literal: To their northwest were remnants of the Xiongnu, a state especially rich and strong, whose chief was called Bayeji. He raised troops to attack Shelun; Shelun met him on the Egen River and routed him; later they were all annexed by Shelun.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay a wealthy remnant Xiongnu state under the chief Bayeji, who marched against Shelun; Shelun met him on the Egen River, crushed him, and eventually absorbed his people entirely.

sentences.zh: 號為強盛。

translations.literal: They were styled powerful and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: They were accounted a great power on the steppe.

sentences.zh: 隨水草畜牧，其西則焉耆之地，東則朝鮮之地，北則渡沙漠，窮瀚海，南則臨大磧。

translations.literal: They followed water and pasture with their herds. To the west was the land of Yanqi; to the east the land of Korea; to the north they crossed the desert to the far reaches of the Hanhai; to the south they bordered the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: They ranged with their flocks after grass and water: Yanqi lay to the west, Korea to the east, beyond the desert and Hanhai to the north, and the great Gobi to the south.

sentences.zh: 其常所會庭則敦煌、張掖之北。

translations.literal: Their usual assembly court lay north of Dunhuang and Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Their habitual gathering place was north of Dunhuang and Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 小國皆苦其寇抄，羈縻附之，於是自號丘豆伐可汗。

translations.literal: Small states all suffered from their raids; they were bound and attached to him, and thereupon he styled himself Khagan Qiudoufa.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser states groaned under his raids and submitted; he then took the title Khagan Qiudoufa.

sentences.zh: 「丘豆伐」猶魏言駕馭開張也，「可汗」猶魏言皇帝也。

translations.literal: "Qiudoufa" is like the Wei word for "driving and opening wide"; "khagan" is like the Wei word for "emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Qiudoufa means, in Wei parlance, "to drive and expand"; khagan means "emperor."

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕之俗，君及大臣因其行能即為稱號，若中國立諡，既死之後，不復追稱。

translations.literal: Among Rouran custom, the ruler and great ministers received titles according to their conduct and ability, like posthumous names in China, but after death no further titles were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran custom gave the ruler and his ministers living epithets based on their deeds, much like Chinese posthumous titles, but no new title was added after death.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂尚書崔玄伯曰：「蠕蠕之人，昔來號為頑嚚，每來抄掠，駕牸牛奔遁，驅犍牛隨之，牸牛伏不能前。

translations.literal: The Taizu said to the Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Xuanbo: "The Rouran have long been called stupid and obstinate. Whenever they came raiding, they would flee driving cows, with oxen following; the cows would lie down and could not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu told Minister Cui Xuanbo: "The Rouran were always called dull and brutal. When they raided and fled, they drove cows while bullocks followed behind; the cows would drop and refuse to move.

sentences.zh: 異部人有教其以犍牛易之者，蠕蠕曰『其母尚不能行，而況其子』，終於不易，遂為敵所虜。

translations.literal: A man of another tribe advised them to exchange the bullocks for the cows. The Rouran said, 'If the mother cannot walk, how much less the sons?' They would not exchange in the end and were captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Someone from another tribe urged them to leave the bullocks and take only the cows. They replied, 'If the mother cannot walk, how can the sons?' They would not abandon the bullocks and were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 今社崘學中國，立法置戰陳，卒成邊害。

translations.literal: Now Shelun has learned from China, established laws, and set battle formations, and in the end has become a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shelun has taken lessons from China, framed laws, and drilled armies—and has become a lasting scourge on our frontier.

sentences.zh: 道家言聖人生，大盜起，信矣。」

translations.literal: The Daoists say that when a sage is born, great robbers arise—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: The Daoists say that when a sage appears, great robbers arise. How true that is."

sentences.zh: 天興五年，社崘聞太祖征姚興，遂犯塞，入參合陂，南至豺山及善無北澤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Shelun heard that the Taizu was campaigning against Yao Xing and thereupon invaded the frontier, entering Canhe Marsh, south to Mount Chai and the northern marshes of Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year 5, learning that Emperor Daowu was away fighting Yao Xing, Shelun raided the border, pushed to Canhe Marsh, and south as far as Mount Chai and the northern lakes of Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 時遣常山王遵以萬騎追之，不及。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Changshan Zun was sent with ten thousand horsemen in pursuit but did not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changshan Zun was sent after him with ten thousand horse but could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 天賜中，社崘從弟悅代、大那等謀殺社崘而立大那，發覺，大那等來奔。

translations.literal: During Tianci, Shelun's younger cousin Yuedai, Dana, and others plotted to kill Shelun and install Dana; the plot was discovered, and Dana and the others came over to us.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianci era Shelun's cousin Yuedai, Dana, and others conspired to kill Shelun and put Dana on the throne; exposed, Dana and his fellows fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 以大那為冠軍將軍、西平侯，悅代為越騎校尉、易陽子。

translations.literal: Dana was made General Who Conquers the Champions and Marquis of Xiping; Yuedai was made Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry and Baron of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dana was appointed General Who Conquers the Champions and Marquis of Xiping; Yuedai became Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry and Baron of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，社崘寇邊，永興元年冬，又犯塞。

translations.literal: In the third summer Shelun raided the border; in the first winter of Yongxing he again violated the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 3 Shelun raided the frontier; in winter of Yongxing year 1 he struck the border again.

sentences.zh: 二年，太宗討之，社崘遁走，道死。

translations.literal: In the second year the Taizong campaigned against him; Shelun fled and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Emperor Mingyuan marched against him; Shelun fled and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 其子度拔年少，未能御眾，部落立社崘弟斛律，號藹苦蓋可汗，魏言姿質美好也。

translations.literal: His son Dubo was young and could not command the masses; the tribes installed Shelun's younger brother Hulu, who styled himself Khagan Aikugai—in Wei speech, "of fine appearance."
translations.idiomatic: His son Dubo was too young to lead; the tribes raised Shelun's brother Hulu as Khagan Aikugai—"comely in bearing," in Wei parlance.

sentences.zh: 斛律北并賀術也骨國，東破譬曆辰部落。

translations.literal: Hulu annexed the northern Heshiye Gu state and to the east defeated the Pilichen tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu absorbed the Heshiye Gu state in the north and broke the Pilichen tribe in the east.

sentences.zh: 三年，斛律宗人悅侯咄觝干等數百人來降。

translations.literal: In the third year several hundred of Hulu's clansmen, including Yuehou, Duogangan, and others, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 several hundred of Hulu's kinsmen, including Yuehou and Duogangan, defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 斛律畏威自守，不敢南侵，北邊安靜。

translations.literal: Hulu feared our might and kept to himself, not daring to invade south; the northern frontier was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu, in awe of Wei power, held his own and did not raid south; the north remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 神瑞元年，與馮跋和親，跋聘斛律女為妻，將為交婚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenrui he entered a marriage alliance with Feng Ba; Ba sought Hulu's daughter as wife and was about to exchange marriages.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenrui year 1 he allied by marriage with Feng Ba of Northern Yan, who sought Hulu's daughter and was to seal the bond with a reciprocal match.

sentences.zh: 斛律長兄子步鹿真謂斛律曰：「女小遠適，憂思生疾，可遣大臣樹黎、勿地延等女為媵。

translations.literal: Hulu's elder brother's son Buluzhen said to Hulu: "The girl is young and going far to marry; worry and longing may bring illness. You could send the daughters of your ministers Shuli and Wudiyan as attendants."
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen, nephew of Hulu's elder brother, urged him: "She is young and going far abroad; homesickness may make her ill. Send the daughters of ministers Shuli and Wudiyan as her attendants."

sentences.zh: 」斛律不許。

translations.literal: " Hulu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Hulu refused.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真出，謂樹黎等曰：「斛律欲令汝女為媵，遠至他國。

translations.literal: Buluzhen went out and said to Shuli and the others: "Hulu intends to make your daughters attendants and send them far to another country."
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen left and told Shuli and the rest: "Hulu means to send your daughters as attendants to a foreign land."

sentences.zh: 」黎遂共結謀，令勇士夜就斛律穹廬，候伺其出執之，與女俱嬪于和龍。

translations.literal: " Shuli and the others then joined in a plot, sending warriors by night to Hulu's yurt; when he came out they seized him and, with his daughter, presented them as brides at Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuli and his allies then conspired: at night warriors surrounded Hulu's tent, seized him when he emerged, and sent him and his daughter to Helong as bride-gifts.

sentences.zh: 乃立步鹿真。

translations.literal: They thereupon installed Buluzhen.
translations.idiomatic: They then raised Buluzhen to the throne.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真立，委政樹黎。

translations.literal: When Buluzhen was established, he entrusted government to Shuli.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen handed the reins of power to Shuli.

sentences.zh: 初，高車叱洛侯者叛其渠帥，導社崘破諸部落，社崘德之，以為大人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chiluohou of the Gaoche had rebelled against his tribal chief and guided Shelun in destroying the various tribes; Shelun was grateful and made him a great chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Gaoche leader Chiluohou had turned against his chief and helped Shelun smash rival tribes; Shelun rewarded him with the rank of great chief.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真與社崘子社拔共至叱洛侯家，淫其少妻。

translations.literal: Buluzhen and Shelun's son Sheba together went to Chiluohou's house and violated his young wife.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen and Shelun's son Sheba visited Chiluohou's home and assaulted his young wife.

sentences.zh: 妻告步鹿真，叱洛侯欲舉大檀為主，遺大檀金馬勒為信。

translations.literal: The wife told Buluzhen that Chiluohou intended to raise Datan as lord and had sent Datan a golden horse bridle as token.
translations.idiomatic: She told Buluzhen that Chiluohou meant to make Datan chief and had sent him a golden bridle as pledge.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真聞之，歸發八千騎往圍叱洛侯，叱洛侯焚其珍寶，自刎而死。

translations.literal: When Buluzhen heard this, he returned and sent eight thousand horsemen to surround Chiluohou; Chiluohou burned his treasures and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen rode back with eight thousand horse, besieged Chiluohou, who burned his valuables and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真遂掩大檀，大檀發軍執步鹿真及社拔，絞殺之，乃自立。

translations.literal: Buluzhen then moved against Datan in secret; Datan raised troops, seized Buluzhen and Sheba, strangled them, and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen then struck at Datan, who mobilized, captured Buluzhen and Sheba, strangled them, and took power himself.

sentences.zh: 大檀者，社崘季父僕渾之子，先統別部，鎮於西界，能得眾心，國人推戴之，號牟汗紇升蓋可汗，魏言制勝也。

translations.literal: Datan was the son of Shelun's younger uncle's son Puhun; he had earlier commanded a separate division, garrisoning the western marches, and could win men's hearts. The people raised him and he styled himself Khagan Mouhanheshengai—in Wei speech, "conquering victor."
translations.idiomatic: Datan, son of Shelun's cousin Puhun, had long led a separate division on the western frontier and won the people's loyalty; they acclaimed him Khagan Mouhanheshengai—"he who prevails," in Wei terms.

sentences.zh: 斛律父子既至和龍，馮跋封為上谷侯。

translations.literal: After Hulu and his son reached Helong, Feng Ba enfeoffed them as Marquises of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hulu and his son reached Helong, Feng Ba made them Marquises of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 大檀率眾南徙犯塞，太宗親討之，大檀懼而遁走。

translations.literal: Datan led his masses south, moved camp, and violated the frontier. The Taizong campaigned in person; Datan was afraid and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Datan shifted south and raided the border; Emperor Mingyuan marched in person, and Datan fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 遣山陽侯奚斤等追之，遇寒雪，士眾凍死墮指者十二三。

translations.literal: Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin and others were sent in pursuit; they met bitter snow, and one or two in ten of the troops froze to death or lost fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin, Marquis of Shanyang, and others pursued him through blizzards; a tenth or more of the army froze to death or lost fingers to frostbite.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，世祖即位，大檀聞而大喜，始光元年秋，乃寇雲中。

translations.literal: When the Taizong died and Shizu succeeded, Datan heard and was greatly pleased. In the autumn of the first year of Shiguang he raided Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu took the throne, Datan rejoiced; in autumn of Shiguang year 1 he attacked Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 世祖親討之，三日二夜至雲中。

translations.literal: The Shizu campaigned in person, reaching Yunzhong in three days and two nights.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched against him and reached Yunzhong in three days and two nights.

sentences.zh: 大檀騎圍世祖五十餘重，騎逼馬首，相次如堵焉。

translations.literal: Datan's horsemen surrounded the Shizu in more than fifty rings; riders pressed to the horses' heads, rank upon rank like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's cavalry ringed the emperor in fifty-odd lines, horsemen pressing nose to bridle in ranks dense as a wall.

sentences.zh: 士卒大懼，世祖顏色自若，眾情乃安。

translations.literal: The soldiers were greatly afraid; the Shizu's countenance remained calm, and the troops' spirits were steadied.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were terrified, but the emperor's face stayed calm and the army steadied.

sentences.zh: 先是，大檀弟大那與社崘爭國，敗而來奔。

translations.literal: Earlier, Datan's younger brother Dana had contended with Shelun for the realm, been defeated, and come over to us.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Datan's brother Dana had lost a struggle with Shelun for power and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 大檀以大那子於陟斤為部帥，軍士射於陟斤殺之，大檀恐，乃還。

translations.literal: Datan had made Dana's son Yuzhijin tribal chief; soldiers shot and killed Yuzhijin. Datan was afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Datan had installed Dana's son Yuzhijin as a tribal chief, but Wei soldiers shot Yuzhijin dead; Datan took fright and retreated.

sentences.zh: 二年，世祖大舉征之，東西五道並進：平陽王長孫翰等從黑漠，汝陰公長孫道生從白黑兩漠間，車駕從中道，東平公娥清次西從粟園，宜城王奚斤、將軍安原等西道從爾寒山。

translations.literal: In the second year the Shizu launched a great campaign against him, advancing on five routes east and west: Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others from the Black Desert; Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng between the White and Black Deserts; the imperial carriage on the central route; Duke of Dongping E Qing second west from Suyuan; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin, General Anyuan, and others on the western route from Erhan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Emperor Taiwu mounted a major expedition on five columns: Changsun Han from the Black Desert, Changsun Daosheng through the belt between the White and Black Deserts, the emperor on the center, E Qing west from Suyuan, and Xi Jin and Anyuan from Erhan Mountain in the west.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至漠南，舍輜重，輕騎齎十五日糧，絕漠討之，大檀部落駭驚北走。

translations.literal: The armies reached south of the desert, abandoned baggage, and with light cavalry carrying fifteen days' rations crossed the desert to attack; Datan's tribes were terrified and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The armies reached the southern Gobi, left their baggage train, and with light horse carrying fifteen days' grain crossed the desert; Datan's people fled north in panic.

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年八月，大檀遣子將騎萬餘人入塞，殺掠邊人而走。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shenlu, Datan sent his son with more than ten thousand horsemen into the frontier, killed and plundered border people, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Shenlu year 1 Datan's son led ten thousand horse into the border, killed and looted, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 附國高車追擊破之。

translations.literal: The subject Gaoche pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Subject Gaoche forces pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 自廣寧還，[5]追之不及。

translations.literal: Returning from Guangning, [5] the pursuit did not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from Guangning, [5] pursuers failed to catch them.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，世祖練兵于南郊，將襲大檀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year the Shizu drilled troops at the southern suburb, intending to strike Datan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 the emperor drilled at the southern suburb, preparing to strike Datan.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣皆不願行，術士張淵、徐辯以天文說止世祖，世祖從崔浩計而行。

translations.literal: The high ministers all wished not to go. The diviners Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian used astronomy to urge the Shizu to stop; the Shizu followed Cui Hao's plan and went.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged against the campaign; diviners Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian cited the stars to dissuade him, but he followed Cui Hao's advice and marched.

sentences.zh: 會江南使還，稱劉義隆欲犯河南，謂行人曰：「汝疾還告魏主，歸我河南地，即當罷兵，不然盡我將士之力。

translations.literal: It happened that envoys from the south returned, reporting that Liu Yilong intended to invade Henan, and said to our messenger: "Return quickly and tell the Wei ruler: restore our Henan lands and we will cease arms; otherwise we will exert all our generals' and soldiers' strength."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the south reported that Liu Yilong of Song meant to attack Henan and told our envoy: "Hurry back and tell the Wei emperor: return our lands south of the Yellow River and we will stand down—or we will throw our full strength against you."

sentences.zh: 」世祖聞而大笑，告公卿曰：「龜鼈小竪，自救不暇，何能為也。

translations.literal: " The Shizu heard and laughed greatly, telling the ministers: "That turtle-and-serpent stripling can scarcely save himself—what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and told his ministers: "That turtle of a boy can barely save himself—what threat is he?

sentences.zh: 就使能來，若不先滅蠕蠕，便是坐待寇至，腹背受敵，非上策也。

translations.literal: Even if he could come, if we do not first destroy the Rouran, we would simply sit waiting for the enemy to arrive, attacked front and rear—that is no superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he did come, failing to crush the Rouran first would leave us caught between two foes—that is no sound plan.

sentences.zh: 吾行決矣。

translations.literal: My march is decided."
translations.idiomatic: I am going."

sentences.zh: 」於是車駕出東道向黑山，平陽王長孫翰從西道向大娥山，同會賊庭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the imperial carriage set out on the eastern route toward Black Mountain; Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han took the western route toward Great E Mountain, meeting at the enemy's court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the eastern road toward Black Mountain while Changsun Han marched west toward Great E Mountain to rendezvous at the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 五月，次于沙漠南，舍輜重輕襲之，至栗水，大檀眾西奔。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he halted south of the desert, abandoned baggage for a light strike, reached Li River, and Datan's masses fled west.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he camped south of the desert, left the baggage train for a swift strike, reached the Li River, and Datan's host fled west.

sentences.zh: 弟匹黎先典東落，將赴大檀，遇翰軍，翰縱騎擊之，殺其大人數百。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pili had earlier governed the eastern tribes and was about to join Datan; he met Han's army. Han loosed his horsemen and struck, killing several hundred of their great chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's brother Pili, who held the eastern tribes, was marching to join him when he met Han's force; Han charged and killed hundreds of their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 大檀聞之震怖，將其族黨，焚燒廬舍，絕跡西走，莫知所至。

translations.literal: Datan heard and was struck with terror; he led his clansmen, burned their dwellings, vanished westward without trace, and none knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: Datan was terrified; he burned his camps and vanished west with his kin—no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 於是國落四散，竄伏山谷，畜產布野，無人收視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribal settlements scattered in all directions, hiding in valleys; livestock lay across the wilds with no one to tend them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes scattered into the hills; herds roamed the steppe untended.

sentences.zh: 世祖緣栗水西行，過漢將竇憲故壘。

translations.literal: The Shizu followed the Li River west, passing the old encampment of the Han general Dou Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched west along the Li River, passing the old camp of the Han general Dou Xian.

sentences.zh: 六月，車駕次於兔園水，去平城三千七百里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the imperial carriage halted at Tuyuan River, three thousand seven hundred li from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court camped at Tuyuan River, thirty-seven hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 分軍搜討，東至瀚海，西接張掖水，北渡燕然山，東西五千餘里，南北三千里。

translations.literal: The army was divided to search and subdue: east to the Hanhai, west to Zhangye River, north crossing Mount Yanran—more than five thousand li east to west and three thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Columns swept the steppe from the Hanhai in the east to the Zhangye River in the west and Mount Yanran in the north—a front of five thousand li by three thousand.

sentences.zh: 高車諸部殺大檀種類，前後歸降三十餘萬，俘獲首虜及戎馬百餘萬匹。

translations.literal: The various Gaoche tribes killed Datan's kinsmen; in all more than three hundred thousand submitted, and captives and war horses taken numbered more than a million head.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche tribes slew Datan's kin; more than three hundred thousand submitted in all, with over a million heads of captives and horses taken.

sentences.zh: 八月，世祖聞東部高車屯巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，去官軍千餘里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Emperor Taiwu heard that the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sini Po with very many people and livestock, more than a thousand li from the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Emperor Taiwu learned that eastern Gaoche tribes were camped at Sini Po with vast herds and households, over a thousand li from his army.

sentences.zh: 遂遣左僕射安原等往討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Left Vice Director Anyuan and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched Left Vice Director Anyuan and others to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 暨巳尼陂，高車諸部望軍降者數十萬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Sini Po, the various Gaoche tribes who saw the army and submitted numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Sini Po, Gaoche tribes who sighted the columns and surrendered numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 大檀部落衰弱，因發疾而死，子吳提立，號敕連可汗，魏言神聖也。

translations.literal: Datan's tribe had weakened; he died of a sudden illness, and his son Wuti succeeded him, styling himself Khagan Chilian—in Wei speech, "sacred."
translations.idiomatic: Datan's power had waned; he died of illness, and his son Wuti took the throne as Khagan Chilian—"sacred," in Wei parlance.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year four they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，北鄙候騎獲吳提南偏邏者二十餘人，世祖賜之衣服，遣歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, northern frontier scout horsemen had captured more than twenty of Wuti's southern patrol guards; Emperor Taiwu gave them clothing and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier scouts on the northern marches had seized more than twenty of Wuti's southern patrolmen; Emperor Taiwu clothed them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 吳提上下感德，故朝貢焉。

translations.literal: Wuti's court high and low were moved by his virtue, and therefore they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti and his followers were touched by this kindness, and so they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖厚賓其使而遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu richly entertained their envoys and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu lavished gifts on the envoys and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 延和三年二月，以吳提尚西海公主，又遣使人納吳提妹為夫人，又進為左昭儀。

translations.literal: In the second month of Yanhe year three Wuti was married to the Princess of Xihai; envoys were also sent to take Wuti's younger sister as consort, and she was later advanced to Left Brilliant Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yanhe year three Wuti wed the Princess of Xihai; Wei envoys also received his sister as consort, later promoting her to Left Brilliant Consort.

sentences.zh: 吳提遣其兄禿鹿傀及左右數百人來朝，獻馬二千匹，世祖大悅，班賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Wuti sent his elder brother Tuluigui and several hundred attendants to court, presenting two thousand horses; Emperor Taiwu was greatly pleased and distributed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti sent his brother Tuluigui with several hundred retainers to court, offering two thousand horses; Emperor Taiwu was delighted and rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 至太延二年，乃絕和犯塞。

translations.literal: By Taiyan year two they broke the peace and raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: By Taiyan year two they broke relations and raided the border.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕幸五原，遂征之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the imperial carriage visited Wuyuan and then campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the emperor went to Wuyuan and marched against them.

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕、河東公賀多羅督十五將出東道，永昌王健、宜都王穆壽督十五將出西道，車駕出中道。

translations.literal: Prince of Le Ping Pi and Duke of Hedong Heduoluo directed fifteen generals on the eastern route; Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and Prince of Yidu Mu Shou directed fifteen on the western route; the imperial carriage took the center route.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Le Ping Pi and Duke of Hedong Heduoluo led fifteen generals east; Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and Prince of Yidu Mu Shou led fifteen west; the emperor took the center.

sentences.zh: 至浚稽山，分中道復為二道，陳留王崇從大澤向涿邪山，車駕從浚稽北向天山。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Xunji, the center column was again split in two: Prince of Chenliu Chong went from the Great Marsh toward Mount Zhuoye; the imperial carriage went north from Xunji toward Heavenly Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Xunji the center force split again: Prince of Chenliu Chong marched from the Great Marsh toward Mount Zhuoye while the emperor turned north from Xunji toward Heavenly Mountain.

sentences.zh: 西登白阜，刻石記行，不見蠕蠕而還。

translations.literal: Westward they ascended Mount Baifu, carved stone recording the march, saw no Rouran, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They climbed Mount Baifu in the west, carved an inscription of the march, found no Rouran, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時漠北大旱，無水草，軍馬多死。

translations.literal: At that time the far north suffered great drought, without water or grass; many army horses died.
translations.idiomatic: The northern steppe was gripped by drought; water and fodder failed, and countless army horses perished.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西伐沮渠牧犍，宜都王穆壽輔景穆居守，長樂王嵇敬、建寧王崇二萬人鎮漠南，以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage campaigned west against Juqu Mujian; Prince of Yidu Mu Shou assisted Crown Prince Jingmu in guarding the capital; Prince of Changle Ji Jing and Prince of Jianning Chong with twenty thousand men garrisoned south of the desert to guard against Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In year five the emperor marched west against Juqu Mujian; Prince of Yidu Mu Shou aided Crown Prince Jingmu in the capital while Prince of Changle Ji Jing and Prince of Jianning Chong held the southern desert with twenty thousand men against Rouran.

sentences.zh: 吳提果犯塞，壽素不設備，賊至七介山，京邑大駭，爭奔中城。

translations.literal: Wuti did raid the frontier; Mu Shou had never made preparations—when the bandits reached Mount Qijie the capital was greatly alarmed and people rushed into the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti struck the border as expected; Mu Shou had made no defense—when raiders reached Mount Qijie the capital panicked and crowds fled into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 司空長孫道生拒之於吐頹山。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng blocked them at Mount Tuhui.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng met them at Mount Tuhui and held them off.

sentences.zh: 吳提之寇也，留其兄乞列歸與北鎮諸軍相守，敬、崇等破乞列歸于陰山之北，獲之。

translations.literal: In Wuti's raid he left his elder brother Qiliegui to hold against the northern garrison forces; Ji Jing and Chong and others defeated Qiliegui north of Yin Mountain and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuti's invasion he left his brother Qiliegui to face the northern garrisons; Ji Jing and Chong routed Qiliegui north of Yin Mountain and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 乞列歸歎曰：「沮渠陷我也。

translations.literal: Qiliegui sighed: "The Juqu have ruined me."
translations.idiomatic: Qiliegui lamented, "The Juqu have undone me."

sentences.zh: 」獲其伯父他吾無鹿胡及其將帥五百人，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: They captured his uncle Tawuwuluhu and more than five hundred of his officers, and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his uncle Tawuwuluhu and over five hundred commanders, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 吳提聞而遁走，道生追之，至于漠南而還。

translations.literal: Wuti heard and fled; Daosheng pursued to south of the desert and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti fled on the news; Daosheng pursued him to the southern desert and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 真君四年，車駕幸漠南，分四道：樂安王範、建寧王崇各統十五將出東道，樂平王督十五將出西道，[6]車駕出中道，中山王辰領十五將為中軍後繼。

translations.literal: In Zhenjun year four the imperial carriage visited the southern desert and divided into four routes: Prince of Le'an Fan and Prince of Jianning Chong each commanded fifteen generals on the eastern route; the Prince of Le Ping directed fifteen generals on the western route; [6] the imperial carriage took the center route, and Prince of Zhongshan Chen led fifteen generals as rear guard of the center army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun year four the emperor went to the southern desert in four columns: Princes of Le'an Fan and Jianning Chong each led fifteen generals east; the Prince of Le Ping led fifteen west; [6] the emperor took the center, with Prince of Zhongshan Chen and fifteen generals as central reserve.

sentences.zh: 車駕至鹿渾谷，與賊將遇，吳提遁走，追至頞根河，擊破之。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Luhun Valley, met the enemy commanders, Wuti fled, they pursued to Ergen River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Luhun Valley the emperor met enemy leaders; Wuti fled, was chased to the Ergen River, and was broken.

sentences.zh: 車駕至石水而還。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Shishui and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor advanced to Shishui and turned back.

sentences.zh: 五年，復幸漠南，欲襲吳提，吳提遠遁，乃還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again visited the southern desert, intending to strike Wuti; Wuti fled far away, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he again went to the southern desert to ambush Wuti, but Wuti had fled deep into the steppe, so he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吳提死，子吐賀真立，號處可汗，魏言唯也。

translations.literal: Wuti died; his son Tuhezhen succeeded, styling himself Khagan Chu—in Wei speech, "sole."
translations.idiomatic: Wuti died and his son Tuhezhen became Khagan Chu—"sole," in Wei terms.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，車駕北伐，高涼王那出東道，[7]略陽王羯兒出西道，車駕與景穆自中道出涿邪山。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Gaoliang Na took the eastern route; [7] Prince of Lueyang Jie'er took the western route; the imperial carriage and Jingmu themselves took the center route from Mount Zhuoye.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year ten the emperor marched north: Prince of Gaoliang Na on the east, [7] Prince of Lueyang Jie'er on the west, while the emperor and Crown Prince Jingmu advanced through the center from Mount Zhuoye.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真別部帥尒綿他拔等率千餘家來降。

translations.literal: Branch chiefs of Tuhezhen such as Ermiantaba led more than a thousand households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen subordinate chiefs including Ermiantaba brought over a thousand households to surrender.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍行數千里，吐賀真新立，恐懼遠遁。

translations.literal: At that time the army had marched several thousand li; Tuhezhen had only just succeeded and, in fear, fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The army had marched thousands of li; Tuhezhen, newly enthroned, fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 九月，車駕北伐，高涼王那出東道，略陽王羯兒出中道，與諸軍期會於地弗池。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Gaoliang Na took the eastern route; Prince of Lueyang Jie'er took the center route, to rendezvous with the other armies at Difu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor marched north again: Na east, Jie'er in the center, all to meet at Difu Pool.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真悉國精銳，軍資甚盛，圍那數十重，那掘長圍堅守，相持數日。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen mustered the elite of the whole state with abundant supplies; he surrounded Na in dozens of rings. Na dug a long encirclement and held firm; they faced each other for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen threw his best troops and stores against Na, encircling him layer upon layer; Na threw up a deep ring of defenses and held for days.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真數挑戰，輒不利，以那眾少而固，疑大軍將至，解圍夜遁。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen repeatedly challenged battle but was always at a disadvantage; because Na's force was few yet firm, he suspected the great army was about to arrive, lifted the siege, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen attacked again and again without success; seeing Na's small but stubborn force, he feared the main army was near, broke the siege, and slipped away by night.

sentences.zh: 那引軍追之，九日九夜，吐賀真益懼，棄輜重，踰穹隆嶺遠遁。

translations.literal: Na led his army in pursuit for nine days and nine nights; Tuhezhen grew still more afraid, abandoned his baggage, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Na pursued nine days and nights; Tuhezhen, in growing panic, abandoned his train, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 那收其輜重，引軍還，與車駕會於廣澤。

translations.literal: Na collected the baggage and led his army back, meeting the imperial carriage at Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Na gathered the abandoned stores and rejoined the emperor at Guangze.

sentences.zh: 略陽王羯兒盡收其人戶畜產百餘萬。

translations.literal: Prince of Lueyang Jie'er collected all their households, people, and livestock—more than a million head.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lueyang Jie'er took more than a million people and animals.

sentences.zh: 自是吐賀真遂單弱，遠竄，邊疆息警矣。

translations.literal: From this Tuhezhen grew isolated and weak, fled far away, and frontier alarms ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen was left isolated and driven far north; the border knew peace.

sentences.zh: 太安四年，車駕北征，騎十萬，車十五萬兩，旌旗千里，遂渡大漠。

translations.literal: In Tai'an year four the imperial carriage campaigned north with one hundred thousand horsemen and one hundred fifty thousand carts; banners stretched for a thousand li, and they crossed the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an year four the emperor marched north with a hundred thousand cavalry and a hundred fifty thousand wagons, banners filling the horizon for a thousand li, and crossed the great Gobi.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真遠遁，其莫弗烏朱駕頹率眾數千落來降，乃刊石記功而還。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen fled far away; his mofu Wuzhu Jiatui led several thousand tribes to submit; they carved stone recording merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen fled; his minister Wuzhu Jiatui surrendered with several thousand clans; the army carved a victory inscription and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世祖征伐之後，[8]意存休息，蠕蠕亦怖威北竄，不敢復南。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taiwu's campaigns, [8] his intent was to rest; the Rouran also feared his might, fled north, and dared not come south again.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu's wars, [8] he sought repose; the Rouran, cowed by his power, fled north and no longer dared raid the south.

sentences.zh: 和平五年，吐賀真死，子予成立，號受羅部真可汗，魏言惠也。

translations.literal: In Heping year five Tuhezhen died; his son Yucheng succeeded, styling himself Khagan Shouluobuzhen—in Wei speech, "kind."
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year five Tuhezhen died; his son Yucheng became Khagan Shouluobuzhen—"benevolent," in Wei parlance.

sentences.zh: 自稱永康元年，率部侵塞，北鎮遊軍大破其眾。

translations.literal: He styled his reign Yongkang year one, led his tribes to raid the frontier, and the northern garrisons' patrol troops greatly defeated his host.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed Yongkang year one, raided the border with his tribes, and northern patrols routed his army.

sentences.zh: 皇興四年，予成犯塞，車駕北討。

translations.literal: In Huangxing year four Yucheng raided the frontier; the imperial carriage campaigned north to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing year four Yucheng struck the border; the emperor marched north against him.

sentences.zh: 京兆王子推、東陽公元丕督諸軍出西道，任城王雲等督軍出東道，汝陰王賜、濟南公羅烏拔督軍為前鋒，隴西王源賀督諸軍為後繼。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Zitui and Prince of Dongyang Yuan Pi directed the armies on the western route; Prince of Rencheng Yun and others directed armies on the eastern route; Prince of Runan Ci and Duke of Jinan Luo Wuba directed the vanguard; Prince of Longxi Yuan He directed the armies as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Zitui and Prince of Dongyang Yuan Pi led the western wing; Prince of Rencheng Yun led the east; Princes of Runan Ci and Duke of Jinan Luo Wuba formed the van; Prince of Longxi Yuan He commanded the rear.

sentences.zh: 諸將會車駕于女水之濱，顯祖親誓眾，詔諸將曰：「用兵在奇不在眾也，卿等為朕力戰，方略已在朕心。

translations.literal: The generals met the imperial carriage on the banks of the Nü River; Emperor Xianzu personally swore the troops and issued an edict to the generals: "In warfare the extraordinary matters, not the multitude; you shall fight for me with all your strength—the strategy is already in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders joined the emperor on the Nü River; Emperor Xianzu took the oath himself and told them, "Victory lies in surprise, not numbers—you shall fight for me with all you have; the plan is already set.

sentences.zh: 」乃選精兵五千人挑戰，多設奇兵以惑之。

translations.literal: " He then selected five thousand elite troops to challenge battle and set many feint forces to confuse the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent five thousand picked men to provoke battle while spreading decoys to bewilder the foe.

sentences.zh: 虜眾奔潰，逐北三十餘里，斬首五萬級，降者萬餘人，戎馬器械不可稱計。

translations.literal: The enemy masses broke and fled; they pursued north for more than thirty li, beheaded fifty thousand, received more than ten thousand submissions, and war horses and equipment were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians collapsed; the pursuit ran thirty li north, taking fifty thousand heads and ten thousand surrenders, with horses and gear beyond tally.

sentences.zh: 旬有九日，往返六千餘里，改女水曰武川，遂作北征頌，刊石紀功。

translations.literal: In nineteen days they went and returned more than six thousand li; they renamed the Nü River Wuchuan, composed a eulogy of the northern campaign, and carved stone recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen days and six thousand li there and back; the Nü River was renamed Wuchuan, a northern campaign hymn written, and victory carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 延興五年，予成求通婚娉，有司以予成數犯邊塞，請絕其使，發兵討之。

translations.literal: In Yanxing year five Yucheng sought a marriage alliance; the responsible offices, because Yucheng had repeatedly raided the frontier, asked to cut off his envoys and send troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year five Yucheng asked to marry; officials, citing his repeated border raids, urged rejecting his envoys and marching against him.

sentences.zh: 顯祖曰：「蠕蠕譬若禽獸，貪而亡義，朕要當以信誠待物，不可抑絕也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu said, "The Rouran are like birds and beasts—greedy and without righteousness; I must nevertheless treat all parties with trust and sincerity and cannot simply cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu declared, "The Rouran are no better than beasts: greedy and faithless. Yet I mean to meet every people with sincerity and trust; their overtures cannot simply be refused."

sentences.zh: 予成知悔前非，遣使請和，求結姻援，安可孤其款意？

translations.literal: Yucheng knows his former errors and regrets them; he has sent envoys to sue for peace and seeks a marriage alliance—how can we leave his earnest intent unanswered?
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng has recognized his past misdeeds and sent envoys suing for peace, asking for a marriage tie—how could we spurn such a sincere approach?

sentences.zh: 」乃詔報曰：「所論婚事，今始一反，尋覽事理，未允厥中。

translations.literal: " Therefore an edict in reply said, "As to the marriage proposed, the matter has only just been raised; on reflection, the circumstances do not yet fall within what is proper."
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued a reply: "The marriage you propose has only this moment been broached; weighing the circumstances, it still falls short of what is fitting."

sentences.zh: 夫男而下女，爻象所明，初婚之吉，敦崇禮娉，君子所以重人倫之本。

translations.literal: The noble takes the woman in marriage and does not place the woman above the man—this the hexagrams make plain; the good fortune of first marriage lies in honoring betrothal rites, for thereby the noble weighs the root of human relations."
translations.idiomatic: "A husband takes a wife and does not rank her above him—the hexagrams make this clear. The blessing of a first marriage rests on honoring betrothal rites; that is how gentlemen uphold the foundations of kinship."

sentences.zh: 不敬其初，令終難矣。

translations.literal: If the beginning is not respected, a proper end will be hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Disrespect at the outset makes a sound outcome all but impossible."

sentences.zh: 」予成每懷譎詐，終顯祖世，更不求婚。

translations.literal: " Yucheng ever harbored treachery; throughout Emperor Xianzu's reign he never again sought marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Yucheng continued to scheme deceitfully, and for the rest of Emperor Xianzu's reign never again asked for a marriage.

sentences.zh: 太和元年四月，遣莫何去汾比拔等來獻良馬、貂裘，比拔等稱伏承天朝珍寶華麗甚積，求一觀之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Taihe, Mohequfen Biba and others were sent to present fine horses and sable pelts; Biba and his party said they bowed before the Heavenly Dynasty's accumulated splendid treasures and asked to view them once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Taihe year (477) the Rouran sent Mohequfen Biba and others with fine horses and sable pelts. Biba's party declared themselves awed by the Son of Heaven's store of treasures and begged a single viewing.

sentences.zh: 乃敕有司出御府珍玩金玉、文繡器物，御廐文馬、奇禽、異獸，及人間所宜用者列之京肆，令其歷觀焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the offices concerned to bring out from the imperial treasury jewels, gold and jade, embroidered vessels, from the imperial stables patterned horses, rare birds and strange beasts, and goods of everyday use in the realm, array them in the capital markets, and have them pass through and view them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the ministries to display in the capital markets treasures from the imperial vaults—gold, jade, brocades, painted mounts from the imperial studs, exotic birds and beasts, and ordinary goods fit for trade—and let the envoys tour the showcase.

sentences.zh: 比拔見之，自相謂曰：「大國富麗，一生所未見也。

translations.literal: When Biba saw them, they said among themselves, "The great state is rich and resplendent—what we have not seen in a lifetime."
translations.idiomatic: Biba and his companions marveled among themselves: "This great realm is staggeringly rich—nothing in our lives has prepared us for the sight."

sentences.zh: 」二年二月，又遣比拔等朝貢，尋復請婚焉。

translations.literal: " In the second year, second month, Biba and others were again sent on tribute; shortly afterward they once more requested marriage.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year, in the second month, Biba and his party returned with tribute, and soon pressed the marriage request again.

sentences.zh: 高祖志存招納，許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, intent on winning men over, assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, determined to win them to allegiance, granted his consent.

sentences.zh: 予成雖歲貢不絕，而款約不著，婚事亦停。

translations.literal: Though Yucheng's yearly tribute never ceased, the terms of good faith were never set down, and the marriage also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng kept sending annual tribute, but no binding pact was concluded and the marriage plans came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 九年，予成死，子豆崘立，號伏古敦可汗，[9]魏言恒也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Yucheng died; his son Douluon succeeded, styling himself Khan Fugudun ([9]: Cefuyuanguo j. 996 reads 名 for 古; Zizhi Tongjian j. 136 agrees; Hu Sansheng cites Wei Shou, "Khan Fumindun, which in Wei speech means constancy"; Sima Guang and Hu Sansheng's Wei Shu and Beishi texts read 名 like Cefuyuanguo—古 is likely corrupt), which in Wei speech means constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Yucheng died and Douluon succeeded as khan, styled Fugudun ([9] collation: the Cefuyuanguo and Zizhi Tongjian read 伏名敦 "Fumindun," as in Wei Shou per Hu Sansheng—伏古敦's 古 is probably a corruption of 名), glossed in Wei parlance as "constancy."

sentences.zh: 自稱太平元年。

translations.literal: He styled himself the first year of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted the era name Taiping ("Great Peace"), year one.

sentences.zh: 豆崘性殘暴好殺，其臣侯醫垔、石洛候數以忠言諫之，又勸與國通和，勿侵中國。

translations.literal: Douluon was by nature cruel and fond of killing; his ministers Hou Yiai and Shiluohou repeatedly admonished him with loyal words and also urged peace with the state and that he not raid China.
translations.idiomatic: Douluon was brutal and bloodthirsty. His ministers Hou Yiai and Shiluohou pled with him to keep faith with the court and cease raiding China.

sentences.zh: 豆崘怒，誣石洛候謀反，殺之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Douluon grew angry, accused Shiluohou of plotting rebellion, killed him, and exterminated three generations of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Douluon charged Shiluohou with treason, executed him, and wiped out three degrees of kin.

sentences.zh: 十六年八月，高祖遣陽平王頤、左僕射陸叡並為都督，領軍斛律桓等十二將七萬騎討豆崘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year, Emperor Xiaowen sent Prince Yangping Yi and Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat Lu Rui, both as grand marshals, with the army commander Hulu Huan and twelve other generals at the head of seventy thousand horsemen to campaign against Douluon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year (492) Emperor Xiaowen dispatched Prince Yangping Yi and Left Vice-Director Lu Rui as joint commanders, with Hulu Huan and twelve generals leading seventy thousand cavalry against Douluon.

sentences.zh: 部內高車阿伏至羅率眾十餘萬落西走，自立為主。

translations.literal: Within his dominions the Gaoche chief Avozhiluo led more than a hundred thousand tents west in flight and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche leader Avozhiluo led a hundred thousand tents west in revolt and proclaimed himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 豆崘與叔父那蓋為二道追之，豆崘出自浚稽山北而西，那蓋出自金山。

translations.literal: Douluon and his uncle Nagai pursued in two columns—Douluon from north of the Xunji Mountains westward, Nagai from Mount Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Douluon and his uncle Nagai gave chase on two routes: Douluon northwest of the Xunji range, Nagai from Mount Jin.

sentences.zh: 豆崘頻為阿伏至羅所敗，那蓋累有勝捷。

translations.literal: Douluon was repeatedly defeated by Avozhiluo; Nagai won victory after victory.
translations.idiomatic: Avozhiluo routed Douluon again and again while Nagai piled up successes.

sentences.zh: 國人咸以那蓋為天所助，欲推那蓋為主。

translations.literal: The people of the realm all thought Nagai was aided by Heaven and wished to set Nagai up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the confederation men said Heaven favoured Nagai and urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 那蓋不從，眾強之，那蓋曰：「我為臣不可，焉能為主！

translations.literal: Nagai would not consent; the multitude pressed him, and Nagai said, "As a subject it is not permissible—how could I become ruler!"
translations.idiomatic: Nagai refused. When the tribes pressed him he protested, "I am a subject—how dare I become khan!"

sentences.zh: 」眾乃殺豆崘母子，以屍示那蓋，那蓋乃襲位。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the multitude killed Douluon and his mother, showed the corpses to Nagai, and Nagai then succeeded to the position.
translations.idiomatic: " The tribes then slew Douluon and his mother, displayed the bodies before Nagai, and only then did Nagai accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 那蓋號候其伏代庫者可汗，魏言悅樂也。

translations.literal: Nagai styled himself Khan Houqifudaike, which in Wei speech means joy and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Nagai took the title Khan Houqifudaike—"delight" in Wei speech.

sentences.zh: 自稱太安元年。

translations.literal: He styled himself the first year of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the Tai'an era, year one.

sentences.zh: 那蓋死，子伏圖立，號他汗可汗，魏言緒也。

translations.literal: When Nagai died, his son Futu succeeded, styling himself Khan Tahhan, which in Wei speech means beginning or thread.
translations.idiomatic: Nagai's son Futu succeeded, styling himself Khan Tahhan—"origins" in Wei parlance.

sentences.zh: 自稱始平元年。

translations.literal: He styled himself the first year of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted the era name Shiping ("Beginning Peace"), year one.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，伏圖遣使紇奚勿六跋朝獻，請求通和。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, Futu sent the envoy Hexi Wuliuoba on tribute and to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhengshi year (506) Futu dispatched Hexi Wuliuoba with tribute and a plea for peace.

sentences.zh: 世宗不報其使，詔有司敕勿六跋曰：「蠕蠕遠祖社崘是大魏叛臣，往者包容，暫時通使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not respond to his envoy and ordered the relevant offices to instruct Wuliuoba, saying, "Shelun, the Rouran's remote ancestor, was a great rebel of Great Wei; in the past you were tolerated and envoys were briefly received.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ignored the embassy and instructed Wuliuoba: "Your distant forebear Shelun was Great Wei's rebel. We indulged you for a time and allowed occasional envoys."

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕衰微，有損疇日，大魏之德，方隆周漢，跨據中原，指清八表。

translations.literal: Now the Rouran are weakened and diminished from former days; Great Wei's virtue rises like Zhou and Han, spanning the Central Plain and aiming to bring order to the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: "Today the Rouran have waned from their former might, while Great Wei's virtue ascends like the Zhou and Han—our dominion holds the Central Plain and points toward pacifying the world."

sentences.zh: 正以江南未平，權寬北掠，通和之事，未容相許。

translations.literal: It is only that the south of the Yangtze is not yet pacified, and we provisionally allow for northern raids; the matter of general peace cannot yet be granted."
translations.idiomatic: "Only because the south remains unconquered do we temporarily overlook your northern raids; a general peace cannot yet be granted."

sentences.zh: 若修藩禮，款誠昭著者，當不孤爾也。

translations.literal: If you repair your vassal courtesy and your sincerity and good faith are manifest, we shall not leave you unsupported."
translations.idiomatic: "Restore proper vassal decorum and show sincere subjecthood clearly, and we shall not fail to reward you."

sentences.zh: 」永平元年，伏圖又遣勿六跋奉函書一封，并獻貂裘，世宗不納，依前喻遣。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yongping, Futu again sent Wuliuoba bearing a letter and also presenting sable pelts; Emperor Xuanwu did not accept them and had him dismissed with the previous instructions.
translations.idiomatic: " In Yongping year one (508) Futu again sent Wuliuoba with a letter and sable tribute; Emperor Xuanwu refused both and dismissed him with the same admonition.

sentences.zh: 伏圖西征高車，為高車王彌俄突所殺，子醜奴立，號豆羅伏跋豆伐可汗，魏言彰制也。

translations.literal: Futu marched west against the Gaoche and was killed by the Gaoche king Mietuo; his son Chounu succeeded, styling himself Khan Douluofubadoufa, which in Wei speech means manifest regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Futu campaigned west against the Gaoche and was killed by their king Mietuo. His son Chounu succeeded as Khan Douluofubadoufa—"manifest regulation" in Wei speech.

sentences.zh: 自稱建昌元年。

translations.literal: He styled himself the first year of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the Jianchang era, year one.

sentences.zh: 永平四年九月，醜奴遣沙門洪宣奉獻珠像。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Yongping, Chounu sent the monk Hong Xuan to present a pearl image.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongping four (511) Chounu sent the monk Hong Xuan with a jeweled Buddha image.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年冬，世宗遣驍騎將軍馬義舒使於醜奴，未發而崩，事遂停寢。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yanchang, Emperor Xuanwu sent Valiant Cavalry General Ma Yishu as envoy to Chounu, but before he set out the emperor died and the mission was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yanchang three (512) Emperor Xuanwu appointed Ma Yishu envoy to Chounu, but the emperor died before he departed and the embassy lapsed.

sentences.zh: 醜奴壯健，善用兵。

translations.literal: Chounu was robust and skilled in the use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu was powerfully built and a capable commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使俟斤尉比建朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he sent envoys Yijin Weibijian on tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of his reign he sent the yijin Weibijian with tribute.

sentences.zh: [10]熙平元年，西征高車大破之，禽其王彌俄突，殺之，盡并叛者，國遂強盛。

translations.literal: [10] In the first year of Xiping, he marched west against the Gaoche, inflicted a great defeat, captured their king Mietuo and killed him, wholly absorbed the rebels, and the state thereupon grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: [10] In the first Xiping year (516), Chounu campaigned west against the Gaoche, shattered them, seized King Mietuo and executed him, absorbed the rebel bands, and his realm grew strong once more.

sentences.zh: 二年，又遣俟斤尉比建、紇奚勿六跋、鞏顧禮等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, Yijin Weibijian, Hexi Wuliuoba, Gong Guli, and others were again sent on tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Weibijian, Wuliuoba, Gong Guli, and others came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年二月，肅宗臨顯陽殿，引顧禮等二十人於殿下，遣中書舍人徐紇宣詔，讓以蠕蠕藩禮不備之意。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shengui, Emperor Xiaozong attended the Xianyang Hall, had Gong Guli and twenty others brought before the steps, and sent Secretariat Gentleman Xu He to proclaim an edict rebuking them for defective Rouran vassal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shengui one (518) Emperor Xiaozong held audience at Xianyang Hall, summoned Gong Guli and twenty companions below the steps, and had Secretariat Gentleman Xu He read an edict faulting their failure in Rouran vassal ritual.

sentences.zh: 初，豆崘之死也，那蓋為主，伏圖納豆崘之妻候呂陵氏，[11]生醜奴、阿那瓌等六人。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Douluon's death Nagai became ruler; Futu took Douluon's wife, Lady Hou Luling ([11]: Tongzhi j. 200 reads Hou 候 as Yi 俟; the Gaoche appendix gives Hou Lülin; Officials and Clans records Chilü later changed to Lü; Yuanhe xingzuan, Tongzhi clans, and Guxing bianzheng read Yilülin; the Yuan Hong epitaph has Yilü Ani—Chi and Yi are close in sound and Hou or Hou is likely a corruption of Yi), who bore Chounu, Anagui, and the rest—six sons in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Douluon died Nagai took the throne, and Futu married his widow Lady Hou Luling ([11] Tongzhi and the Gaoche clan record read 俟 for 候—the graphs 叱/俟 are near in sound and 候 is likely corrupt). She bore Chounu, Anagui, and four more sons—six in all.

sentences.zh: 醜奴立後，忽亡一子，字祖惠，求募不能得。

translations.literal: After Chounu succeeded, a son suddenly disappeared—his courtesy name Zuhui; search and reward could not recover him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chounu was khan a son vanished—Zuhui by courtesy name—and searches with rewards failed to find him.

sentences.zh: 有屋引副升牟妻是豆渾地萬、年二十許，為醫巫，假託神鬼，先常為醜奴所信，出入去來，乃言此兒今在天上，我能呼得。

translations.literal: There was the wife of Wuyin Fushengmou, Yidouhun Diwan, about twenty years old, a physician-shaman who feigned gods and spirits; she had long been trusted by Chounu and came and went freely, and she then said, "This boy is now in Heaven—I can call him back."
translations.idiomatic: A shamanka named Diwan, wife of Fushengmou of the Wuyin clan and some twenty years of age, had long enjoyed Chounu's trust. Feigning communion with spirits, she announced that the lost boy was in Heaven and that she could summon him back.

sentences.zh: 醜奴母子欣悅，後歲仲秋，在大澤中施帳屋，齋潔七日，祈請天上。

translations.literal: Chounu and his mother were delighted; in the mid-autumn of the following year they pitched tents in the great marsh, kept pure fasts for seven days, and prayed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu and his mother rejoiced. The next year's mid-autumn they pitched tents in the great marsh, fasted in ritual purity for seven days, and prayed Heavenward.

sentences.zh: 經一宿，祖惠忽在帳中，自云恒在天上。

translations.literal: After one night Zuhui suddenly appeared in the tent, saying himself that he had constantly been in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After a single night Zuhui appeared in the tent, claiming he had all along dwelt in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 醜奴母子抱之悲喜，大會國人，號地萬為聖女，納為可賀敦，授夫副升牟爵位，賜牛馬羊三千頭。

translations.literal: Chounu and his mother embraced him in joy and grief; a great assembly of the people was held; Diwan was styled Holy Woman, taken in as kehunden; her husband Fushengmou was granted a noble rank and three thousand head of cattle, horses, and sheep were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu and his mother clasped him, laughing and weeping by turns. The tribes assembled; Diwan was hailed Holy Woman and made kehunden (chief consort); Fushengmou received a noble title and three thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 地萬既挾左道，亦有姿色，醜奴甚加重愛，信用其言，亂其國政。

translations.literal: Diwan, relying on heterodox ways and also possessing beauty, Chounu greatly favoured and trusted her words, and she threw state affairs into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Diwan wielded sorcery and beauty alike; Chounu doted on her counsel until state affairs fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 如是積歲，祖惠年長，其母問之，祖惠言：「我恒在地萬家，不嘗上天，上天者地萬教也。

translations.literal: Thus for accumulated years—when Zuhui grew older, his mother questioned him, and Zuhui said, "I have always been at Diwan's home and never went to Heaven; the going to Heaven was what Diwan taught."
translations.idiomatic: Years passed. When Zuhui came of age his mother pressed him, and he confessed, "I never left Diwan's household—Heaven was her invention."

sentences.zh: 」其母具以狀告醜奴，醜奴言：「地萬懸鑒遠事，不可不信，勿用讒言也。

translations.literal: " His mother reported the full circumstances to Chounu, and Chounu said, "Diwan hangs a mirror on distant affairs—you cannot fail to believe her; do not employ slanderous words."
translations.idiomatic: His mother told Chounu everything. Chounu replied, "Diwan sees what happens far away; you must trust her. Pay no heed to malicious talk."

sentences.zh: 」既而地萬恐懼，譖祖惠於醜奴，醜奴陰殺之。

translations.literal: " Before long Diwan grew fearful, slandered Zuhui to Chounu, and Chounu secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Diwan, afraid of exposure, denounced Zuhui to Chounu, who had him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 正光初，醜奴母遣莫何去汾李具列等絞殺地萬，醜奴怒，欲誅具列等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguang era, Chounu's mother sent Mohe to have Fen Li Julie and others strangle Diwan to death; Chounu was angry and wished to execute Julie and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguang reign, Chounu's mother sent Mohe with Fen Li Julie and others to strangle Diwan. Chounu flew into a rage and meant to put Julie and his party to death.

sentences.zh: 又阿至羅侵醜奴，醜奴擊之，軍敗。

translations.literal: Moreover Azhiluo invaded Chounu; Chounu struck at him and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Azhiluo then raided Chounu's territory. Chounu counterattacked and was routed.

sentences.zh: 還，為母與其大臣所殺，立醜奴弟阿那瓌。

translations.literal: On his return he was killed by his mother and her great ministers; they established Chounu's younger brother Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: When he came back, his mother and the chief ministers killed him and set up Chounu's younger brother Anagui as ruler.

sentences.zh: 立經十日，其族兄俟力發示發率眾數萬以伐阿那瓌，阿那瓌戰敗，將弟乙居伐輕騎南走歸國。

translations.literal: Ten days after the enthronement, his clansman elder brother Yifulü Shifa led several tens of thousands to attack Anagui; Anagui was defeated in battle and, taking his younger brother Yijulü on light horse, fled south to submit to the [Wei] state.
translations.idiomatic: Only ten days after Anagui took the throne, his kinsman Yifulü Shifa marched against him with tens of thousands of men. Defeated in battle, Anagui fled south to the Wei court with his brother Yijulü and a light cavalry escort.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌母候呂陵氏及其二弟尋為示發所殺，而阿那瓌未之知也。

translations.literal: Anagui's mother, Lady Hou of the Lüling clan, and his two younger brothers were soon killed by Shifa, yet Anagui did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shifa soon killed Anagui's mother, Lady Hou of the Lüling clan, together with two of his younger brothers—news Anagui had not yet received.

sentences.zh: 九月，阿那瓌將至，肅宗遣兼侍中陸希道為使主，兼散騎常侍孟威為使副，迎勞近畿；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, as Anagui was about to arrive, Emperor Xiaozong sent Acting Attendant-in-Chief Lu Xidao as chief envoy and Acting Palace Attendant Meng Wei as deputy envoy to welcome and comfort him in the near capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with Anagui nearing the capital, Emperor Xiaozong dispatched Lu Xidao, acting attendant-in-chief, as chief envoy and Meng Wei, acting palace attendant, as his deputy to greet and entertain him in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 使司空公、京兆王繼至北中，侍中崔光、黃門郎元纂在近郊，並申宴勞，引至門闕下。

translations.literal: He sent the Duke of the Realm, Prince Ji of Jingzhao, as far as Beizhong; Attendant-in-Chief Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Zuan [met him] in the outer suburbs—all extending banquets of comfort—and led him to below the gate towers.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of the Realm, Prince Ji of Jingzhao, went out to Beizhong; Cui Guang, attendant-in-chief, and Yuan Zuan, yellow gate gentleman, received him nearer the city. Each hosted a feast in his honor before escorting him to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 十月，肅宗臨顯陽殿，引從五品以上清官、皇宗、藩國使客等列於殿庭，王公以下及阿那瓌等入，就庭中北面。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Emperor Xiaozong attended the Xianyang Hall, drew forth from fifth rank and above pure officials, imperial clansmen, and envoys from feudatory states to array in the hall courtyard; princes and dukes downward and Anagui and the rest entered and took position in the courtyard facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor took his seat in the Xianyang Hall. Officials of the fifth rank and above, members of the imperial clan, and foreign envoys lined the courtyard. Anagui and the other guests entered with the princes and dukes and stood facing north in the court.

sentences.zh: 位定，謁者引王公以下升殿，阿那瓌位於藩王之下，又引將命之官及阿那瓌弟并二叔位於羣官之下。

translations.literal: When places were fixed, the usher guided princes and dukes downward up the hall; Anagui was placed below the feudatory kings, and again led the officers bearing credentials together with Anagui's younger brother and two uncles to positions below the mass of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was set, ushers led the princes and dukes up the steps. Anagui was seated below the feudatory kings; his envoys, his younger brother, and two uncles were placed still lower among the officials.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人曹道宣詔勞問，阿那瓌啟云：「陛下優隆，命臣弟叔等升殿預會，但臣有從兄，在北之日，官高於二叔，乞命升殿。

translations.literal: He dispatched Secretariat Gentleman Cao Daoxuan with an edict of inquiry and comfort; Anagui memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty's gracious elevation has ordered my younger brother, uncles, and the rest to ascend the hall and take part in the gathering—but I have a senior cousin who, in the days in the north, held office higher than my two uncles; I beg that he be ordered to ascend the hall."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Daoxuan of the Secretariat was sent to convey the emperor's greetings. Anagui submitted, "Your Majesty has honored my brother, uncles, and kin with seats in the hall. Yet I have a cousin who, when we were still in the north, outranked both uncles. I beg leave for him to join us on the dais."

sentences.zh: 」詔聽之，乃位於阿那瓌弟之下，二叔之上。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it; he was then placed below Anagui's younger brother and above the two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented, and the cousin was seated below Anagui's brother but above the two uncles.

sentences.zh: 宴將罷，阿那瓌執啟立於座後，詔遣舍人常景問所欲言，阿那瓌求詣殿前，詔引之。

translations.literal: As the banquet was about to end, Anagui held his memorial and stood behind his seat; an edict sent Gentleman Chang Jing to ask what he wished to say. Anagui requested to approach before the hall, and an edict led him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the feast Anagui rose behind his seat with a memorial in hand. The emperor sent Chang Jing to ask his request. Anagui asked to speak before the throne and was summoned forward.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌再拜跽曰：「臣先世源由，出於大魏。

translations.literal: Anagui twice bowed and, kneeling, said, "My forebears' origin and source sprang from Great Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Anagui bowed twice and spoke from his knees: "My clan's roots lie in Great Wei."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「朕已具之。

translations.literal: " The edict said, "We already have the full account."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "I am already well informed."

sentences.zh: 」阿那瓌起而言曰：「臣之先，逐草放牧，遂居漠北。

translations.literal: " Anagui rose and spoke, saying, "My ancestors, following the grass to pasture herds, thus dwelt in the desert north."
translations.idiomatic: " Anagui rose and continued, "Our forefathers followed the pastures and came to live on the northern steppe."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「卿言未盡，可具陳之。

translations.literal: " The edict said, "Your words are not yet exhausted—you may set them forth in full."
translations.idiomatic: " "You have not finished," said the emperor. "Speak plainly and at length."

sentences.zh: 」阿那瓌又言曰：「臣先祖以來，世居北土，雖復隔越山津，而乃心慕化；

translations.literal: " Anagui spoke again, saying, "From my first ancestors onward we have dwelt generation after generation in the northern lands; though we were again separated and crossed mountains and fords, yet our hearts admired transformation."
translations.idiomatic: " Anagui went on, "Since the first generations we have lived in the north. Mountains and rivers lay between us, yet our hearts turned toward your civilization."

sentences.zh: 未能時宣者，正以高車悖逆，臣國擾攘，不暇遣使以宣遠誠。
