translations.literal: That we could not at the proper time declare it was just because the Gaoche were perverse and rebellious, my state was disturbed and in turmoil, and we had no leisure to send envoys to declare our distant sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: We could not show that loyalty in good time only because the Gaoche rebelled, our realm fell into turmoil, and we had no peace in which to send envoys bearing our homage from afar.

sentences.zh: 自頃年以前，漸定高車。

translations.literal: From the years just before now, the Gaoche were gradually pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Only in recent years have we slowly brought the Gaoche under control.

sentences.zh: 及臣兄為主，故遣鞏顧禮等使來大魏，實欲虔修藩禮，是以曹道芝北使之日，[12]臣與主兄即遣大臣五人拜受詔命。

translations.literal: When my elder brother became ruler, we therefore sent Gong Gulü and others as envoys to Great Wei, truly wishing devoutly to cultivate feudatory rites; thus on the day Cao Daozhi went north as envoy (collator's note 12: the text above reads "Cao Dao," likely an abbreviated form of the full name, yet "Cao Dao" in juan 75 appears repeatedly without the character zhi), my lord brother and I at once sent five great ministers to bow and receive the edict command.
translations.idiomatic: After my brother took the throne we sent Gong Gulü and others to Great Wei in earnest observance of vassal duty. On the day of Cao Daozhi's mission north (note 12: elsewhere the envoy is named Cao Dao alone, probably a shortened form; records in juan 75 never add zhi), my brother and I immediately dispatched five senior ministers to receive your edict with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 臣兄弟本心未及上徹。

translations.literal: My brothers' and my true hearts had not yet reached upward to penetrate [the throne].
translations.idiomatic: Our loyal intent had not yet reached Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 但高車從而侵暴，中有姦臣，因亂作逆，殺臣兄，立臣為主。

translations.literal: But the Gaoche followed and invaded and ravaged; among us were treacherous ministers who, taking advantage of disorder, rose in rebellion, killed my elder brother, and established me as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Gaoche pressed their attacks. Treacherous ministers seized the chaos, rebelled, murdered my brother, and set me on the throne.

sentences.zh: 裁過旬日，臣以陛下恩慈如天，是故倉卒輕身投國，歸命陛下。

translations.literal: It had barely passed ten days when I, because Your Majesty's gracious kindness was like Heaven, therefore in haste left my body lightly and cast myself on the state, submitting my fate to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Barely ten days later, knowing Your Majesty's mercy to be as vast as heaven, I fled my realm in haste and came to lay my life in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「具卿所陳，理猶未盡，可更言之。

translations.literal: " The edict said, "What you have set forth in full—its principle is still not exhausted; you may speak again."
translations.idiomatic: " "What you have said is still not enough," the emperor replied. "Continue."

sentences.zh: 」阿那瓌再拜受詔，起而言曰：「臣以家難，輕來投闕，老母在彼，萬里分張，本國臣民，皆已迸散。

translations.literal: " Anagui twice bowed, received the edict, rose, and spoke, saying, "I, because of family calamity, lightly came and cast myself on the palace gate; my old mother remains there, separated ten thousand li; the subjects and people of my native state have all already scattered in flight."
translations.idiomatic: " Anagui bowed again, accepted the command, and rose. "Family disaster drove me to throw myself on your mercy. My aged mother is still there, ten thousand li away; the people of my land have fled in every direction."

sentences.zh: 陛下隆恩，有過天地，求乞兵馬，還向本國，誅翦叛逆，收集亡散。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's towering grace surpasses Heaven and Earth; I beg to request troops and horses, return toward my native state, cut down and clip the rebels, and gather the lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace exceeds heaven and earth itself. I beg troops and horses to return home, punish the rebels, and gather my scattered people.

sentences.zh: 陛下慈念，賜借兵馬。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty in compassionate thought bestow and lend troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In your compassion, grant me an army.

sentences.zh: 老母若在，得生相見，以申母子之恩；

translations.literal: If my old mother still lives, I may in life meet her again, thereby extending mother-and-son affection.
translations.idiomatic: If my mother still lives, I may see her again and fulfill a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 如其死也，即得報讎，以雪大耻。

translations.literal: If she has died, then I may at once repay the feud and wash away the great shame.
translations.idiomatic: If she is dead, I may still avenge her and wipe away this grievous disgrace.

sentences.zh: 臣當統臨餘人，奉事陛下，四時之貢，不敢闕絕。

translations.literal: Your subject shall oversee and face the remaining people, serve and attend Your Majesty, and the tribute of the four seasons—I dare not let it be cut off or fail.
translations.idiomatic: I shall rule what subjects remain and serve Your Majesty without fail, offering tribute each season as long as I draw breath.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖顏難覩，敢有披陳，但所欲言者口不能盡言，別有辭啟，謹以仰呈，願垂昭覽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sage countenance is hard to behold; I dare to lay open and declare—but what I wish to say my mouth cannot fully speak; separately there is a written memorial, which I respectfully present looking upward, hoping you will let your bright gaze fall upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Before your sacred presence I dare speak plainly, yet words fail me. I have set the rest in a written memorial, which I humbly submit for your gracious reading.

sentences.zh: 」仍以啟付舍人常景，具以奏聞。

translations.literal: " He thereupon handed the memorial to Gentleman Chang Jing, who set it forth in full and reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave the memorial to Chang Jing, who presented it in full to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋封阿那瓌朔方郡公、蠕蠕王，賜以衣冕，加之軺蓋，祿從、[13]儀衞，同于戚藩。

translations.literal: Soon Anagui was enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang commandery and King of Rouran; he was granted robes and regalia, with carriage canopy added, stipend and retinue (lacuna mark 13 in the received text), ceremonial guard—the same as for kin of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Anagui was made Duke of Shuofang and King of Rouran. He received court robes and insignia, a state carriage with canopy, salary and attendants, and a guard of honor matching those of the emperor's own kin (the received text has a lacuna at note 13).

sentences.zh: 十二月，肅宗以阿那瓌國無定主，思還綏集，啟請切至，詔議之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, because Anagui's state had no fixed ruler and he wished to return and soothe and gather it, his memorial requests were pressing to the utmost; an edict ordered deliberation on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Emperor Xiaozong, seeing Anagui's homeland left without a settled ruler and eager to return and restore order, took his urgent petitions to court for debate.

sentences.zh: 時朝臣意有同異，或言聽還，或言不可。

translations.literal: At that time the court ministers' intentions had sameness and difference—some spoke of approving his return, some spoke that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were divided: some urged letting him go back, others insisted he must not.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉為宰相，阿那瓌私以金百斤貨之，遂歸北。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Yuan Cha served as chief minister; Anagui privately used one hundred jin of gold to bribe him, and thus returned north.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha, general-in-chief and chief minister, was privately paid a hundred jin of gold by Anagui and thereafter allowed him to return north.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，阿那瓌等五十四人請辭，肅宗臨西堂，引見阿那瓌及其伯叔兄弟五人，升階賜坐，遣中書舍人穆弼宣勞。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Anagui and fifty-four others requested leave; Emperor Xiaozong attended the West Hall, summoned Anagui and his father's brothers' sons and brothers—five men—granted them ascent of the steps and bestowed seats, and dispatched Secretariat Gentleman Mu Bi to proclaim comfort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year fifty-four men, Anagui among them, asked leave to depart. The emperor received them in the West Hall, called in Anagui with five uncles and brothers, had them ascend and be seated, and sent Mu Bi of the Secretariat to convey his parting regards.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌等拜辭，詔賜阿那瓌細明光人馬鎧二具，鐵人馬鎧六具；

translations.literal: Anagui and the rest bowed in leave; an edict bestowed on Anagui two suits of fine mingguang armor for man and horse, and six suits of iron man-and-horse armor.
translations.idiomatic: After they bowed their farewells, the emperor granted Anagui two sets of fine mingguang armor for rider and horse and six sets of iron mail for both.

sentences.zh: 露絲銀纏槊二張并白眊，赤漆槊十張并白眊，黑漆槊十張并幡；

translations.literal: Two lances of openwork silk wrapped in silver together with white pennons, ten red-lacquered lances together with white pennons, ten black-lacquered lances together with banners.
translations.idiomatic: two silver-bound spears with openwork silk wrapping and white pennons; ten red-lacquered spears with white pennons; ten black-lacquered spears with streamers.

sentences.zh: 露絲弓二張并箭，朱漆柘弓六張并箭，黑漆弓十張并箭；

translations.literal: Two openwork-silk bows together with arrows, six red-lacquered zhe-wood bows together with arrows, ten black-lacquered bows together with arrows.
translations.idiomatic: two bows wrapped in openwork silk with arrows; six red-lacquered mulberry-wood bows with arrows; ten black-lacquered bows with arrows.

sentences.zh: 赤漆盾六幡并刀，黑漆盾六幡并刀；

translations.literal: Six red-lacquered shields with banners together with blades, six black-lacquered shields with banners together with blades.
translations.idiomatic: six red-lacquered shields with pennants and swords; six black-lacquered shields with pennants and swords.

sentences.zh: 赤漆鼓角二十具；

translations.literal: Twenty sets of red-lacquered drums and horns.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him twenty red-lacquered field drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 五色錦被二領，黃紬被褥三十具；

translations.literal: Two coverlets of five-colored brocade, thirty sets of yellow silk-floss bedding.
translations.idiomatic: two brocade quilts in five colors and thirty sets of yellow silk bedding.

sentences.zh: 私府繡袍一領并帽，內者緋納襖一領；

translations.literal: One embroidered robe from the privy storehouse together with a cap, and for the inner wearer one scarlet lined coat.
translations.idiomatic: one embroidered robe from the imperial wardrobe with its cap, and one scarlet lined jacket for wear beneath.

sentences.zh: 緋袍二十領并帽，內者雜綵千段；

translations.literal: Twenty scarlet robes together with caps, and for inner wear one thousand bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: twenty scarlet robes with caps and a thousand bolts of assorted silks for undergarments.

sentences.zh: 緋納小口袴褶一具，內中宛具；

translations.literal: One set of scarlet lined narrow-cuffed trousers and jacket, with the full inner complement complete.
translations.idiomatic: one fitted suit of scarlet lined trousers and jacket, with full underlayers.

sentences.zh: 紫納大口袴褶一具，內中宛具；

translations.literal: One set of purple lined broad-cuffed trousers and jacket, with the full inner complement complete.
translations.idiomatic: one suit of purple lined trousers and jacket in the loose northern cut, likewise complete with undergarments.

sentences.zh: 百子帳十八具，黃布幕六張；

translations.literal: Eighteen hundred-son tents, six yellow-cloth awnings.
translations.idiomatic: eighteen large camp pavilions and six yellow cloth marquees.

sentences.zh: 新乾飯一百石，麥麨八石，榛麨五石；

translations.literal: new dried grain one hundred shi, wheat meal eight shi, hazel meal five shi;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred shi of newly dried provisions, eight shi of wheat flour, and five shi of hazel flour;

sentences.zh: 銅烏錥四枚，柔鐵烏錥二枚，各受二斛；

translations.literal: copper wujin cauldrons four, wrought-iron wujin cauldrons two, each holding two hu;
translations.idiomatic: four bronze cauldrons and two of wrought iron, each of two-hu capacity;

sentences.zh: 黑漆竹榼四枚，各受二升；

translations.literal: black-lacquered bamboo flasks four, each holding two sheng;
translations.idiomatic: four black-lacquered bamboo flasks of two sheng each;

sentences.zh: 婢二口；

translations.literal: maid-servants two;
translations.idiomatic: two female attendants;

sentences.zh: 父草馬五百匹，駝百二十頭，㹀牛一百頭，羊五千口；

translations.literal: fucao horses five hundred, camels one hundred twenty head, yak-cattle one hundred head, sheep five thousand head;
translations.idiomatic: five hundred herd horses, one hundred and twenty camels, one hundred yaks, and five thousand sheep;

sentences.zh: 朱畫盤器十合；

translations.literal: vermilion-painted platters and vessels ten sets;
translations.idiomatic: ten sets of vermilion-painted dining ware;

sentences.zh: 粟二十萬石。

translations.literal: millet two hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: two hundred thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 至鎮給之。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the fort, grant them.
translations.idiomatic: These were to be issued upon his reaching his post.

sentences.zh: 詔侍中崔光、黃門元纂郭外勞遣。

translations.literal: Edict: Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Zuan shall comfort and escort outside the outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Attendant Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Zuan to see him off beyond the suburbs with honors.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌來奔之後，其從父兄俟力發婆羅門率數萬人入討示發，破之。

translations.literal: After Anagui came in flight, his paternal cousin Yilifa Boluomen led tens of thousands north to attack Shifa and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Anagui had fled to Wei, his cousin Yilifa Boluomen marched north with tens of thousands to strike Shifa and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 示發走奔地豆于，為其所殺。

translations.literal: Shifa fled to the Didouyu and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Shifa fled to the Didouyu confederation and was slain there.

sentences.zh: 推婆羅門為主，號彌偶可社句可汗，魏言安靜也。

translations.literal: They set up Boluomen as ruler, styled Mi'ou Kesheju Khan—in Wei speech, "Tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: They raised Boluomen as khan, giving him the title Mi'ou Kesheju Khan—"Tranquil" in the language of Wei.

sentences.zh: 時安北將軍、懷朔鎮將楊鈞表：「傳聞彼人已立主，是阿那瓌同堂兄弟。

translations.literal: At the time Anbei General and Huaishuo Fort Commander Yang Jun memorialized, "It is reported that they have already set up a ruler there—Anagui's agnatic cousin."
translations.idiomatic: Anbei General and commander of Huaishuo Fort Yang Jun then submitted a memorial: "Word has come that the steppe has a new khan—Anagui's own cousin."

sentences.zh: 夷人獸心，已相君長，恐未肯以殺兄之人，郊迎其弟。

translations.literal: Barbarians have beast-hearts; they have already made one another lord—I fear they will not be willing, with a man who killed his brother, to greet his younger brother in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: These tribesmen think like beasts: they have chosen their chief, and they are unlikely to welcome at the border a younger brother of the man who slew his own kin.

sentences.zh: 輕往虛反，徒損國威，自非廣加兵眾，無以送其入北。

translations.literal: To go lightly and return empty would only damage the state's prestige; unless troops are broadly added, there is no means to send him back into the north.
translations.idiomatic: A token mission that came home empty-handed would only stain our honor; without a substantial escort he cannot be returned to the north.

sentences.zh: 」二月，肅宗詔舊經蠕蠕使者牒云具仁，往喻婆羅門迎阿那瓌復藩之意。

translations.literal: " In the second month Emperor Suzong ordered the former envoy to the Rouran, Dieyun Juren, to go explain to Boluomen the intent to welcome Anagui back to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month Emperor Suzong dispatched Dieyun Juren, who had once served as envoy to the Rouran, to tell Boluomen that Anagui was to be restored to his lands.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門殊自驕慢，無遜避之心，責具仁禮敬，具仁執節不屈。

translations.literal: Boluomen was exceptionally arrogant himself, without a heart of deference; he demanded that Juren show ritual respect, but Juren held to his credentials and would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Boluomen met him with extravagant arrogance, demanding obeisance; Juren stood on his commission and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門遣大官莫何去汾、俟斤丘升頭六人將兵二千隨具仁迎阿那瓌。

translations.literal: Boluomen sent the great officers Mohe Qufen and Yijin Qiufentou and six others to lead two thousand troops to follow Juren in welcoming Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Boluomen sent his great officers Mohe Qufen and Yijin Qiufentou, with six companions and two thousand warriors, to accompany Juren and receive Anagui.

sentences.zh: 五月，具仁還鎮，論彼事勢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Juren returned to the fort and reported on the situation there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Juren came back to the fort and laid out how matters stood on the steppe.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌慮不敢入，表求還京。

translations.literal: Anagui, anxious and daring not to enter, submitted a request to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui, afraid to advance, petitioned to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會婆羅門為高車所逐，率十部落詣涼州歸降，於是蠕蠕數萬相率迎阿那瓌。

translations.literal: It happened that Boluomen was driven out by the Gaoche; he led ten tribes to Liangzhou to submit, and then tens of thousands of Rouran in succession came to welcome Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Boluomen was overthrown by the Gaoche and led ten tribes to surrender at Liangzhou; tens of thousands of Rouran thereupon flocked to welcome Anagui home.

sentences.zh: 七月，阿那瓌啟云：「投化蠕蠕元退社、渾河旃等二人以今月二十六日到鎮，云國土大亂，姓姓別住，迭相抄掠，當今北人鵠望待拯。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Anagui submitted, "The submitted Rouran Yuan Tuishe and Hun Hezhan and two others reached the fort on the twenty-sixth of this month, reporting that the realm is in great disorder—clans dwelling apart, raiding one another in turn; the northerners now crane their necks awaiting deliverance."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Anagui wrote: "Two Rouran who have submitted—Yuan Tuishe and Hun Hezhan—reached the fort on the twenty-sixth. They say the steppe is in chaos: clans scattered, plundering one another. The people of the north watch like geese for rescue."

sentences.zh: 今乞依前恩，賜給精兵一萬，還令督率送臣磧北，撫定荒人，脫蒙所請，事必克濟。

translations.literal: Now I beg, according to your former grace, to be granted elite troops ten thousand, and again be ordered to lead and escort me north of the desert, to pacify and settle the wild peoples—if I receive what I request, the affair will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg again for the ten thousand picked troops you once promised, to lead me beyond the desert and settle the scattered tribes. Grant this, and the task will surely be accomplished."

sentences.zh: 」詔付尚書、門下博議。

translations.literal: " An edict referred the matter to the Secretariat and Chancellery for broad deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The court referred the petition to the Secretariat and Chancellery for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔兼散騎常侍王遵業馳驛宣旨慰阿那瓌，并申賜賚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered Acting Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Wang Zunye to ride post-horses and proclaim the imperial intent to comfort Anagui, and also convey bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Emperor Suzong sent Acting Cavalier Attendant Wang Zunye by relay post to comfort Anagui and confirm his gifts.

sentences.zh: 九月，蠕蠕後主俟匿伐來奔懷朔鎮，阿那瓌兄也，列稱規望乞軍，并請阿那瓌。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the former Rouran lord Hou Nifa came in flight to Huaishuo Fort—Anagui's elder brother—listing his designs and hopes, begging for troops, and also requesting Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the former Rouran khan Hou Nifa, Anagui's elder brother, fled to Huaishuo Fort, laid out his ambitions, begged for an army, and asked that Anagui be sent to join him.

sentences.zh: 十月，錄尚書事高陽王雍、尚書令李崇、侍中侯剛、尚書左僕射元欽、侍中元叉、侍中安豐王延明、吏部尚書元脩義、尚書李彥、給事黃門侍郎元纂、給事黃門侍郎張烈、給事黃門侍郎盧同等奏曰：「竊聞漢立南、北單于，晉有東、西之稱，皆所以相維禦難，為國藩籬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong; Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong; Attendant Hou Gang; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Qin; Attendants Yuan Cha and Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming; Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi; Master of Writing Li Yan; and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, Zhang Lie, and Lu Tong submitted, "We have heard that Han set up Southern and Northern Shanyu, and Jin had Eastern and Western titles—all to support one another against hardship and serve as border fences for the state."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong, who held the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing, together with Li Chong, Hou Gang, Yuan Qin, Yuan Cha, Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming, Yuan Xiuyi, Li Yan, and the Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, Zhang Lie, and Lu Tong memorialized: "We understand that the Han enthroned Southern and Northern Shanyu, and the Jin spoke of Eastern and Western khans—each arrangement meant to brace the realm against trouble and serve as a living frontier."

sentences.zh: 今臣等參議以為懷朔鎮北土名無結山吐若奚泉，敦煌北西海郡即漢晉舊障，二處寬平，原野彌沃。

translations.literal: Now we your subjects, in joint deliberation, hold that north of Huaishuo Fort is a place called Wujie Mountain Turuoqi Spring, and north of Dunhuang the Western Sea Commandery is the old barrier of Han and Jin—both sites broad and level, their plains and marshes exceedingly fertile.
translations.idiomatic: We propose two seats: north of Huaishuo lies the place known as Wujie Mountain and Turuoqi Spring; north of Dunhuang stands Western Sea Commandery, an old Han and Jin frontier. Both are open country, rich in pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌宜置西吐若奚泉，[14]婆羅門宜置西海郡，各令總率部落，收離聚散。

translations.literal: Anagui should be installed at West Turuoqi Spring, [14] Boluomen at Western Sea Commandery—each ordered to command his tribes and gather the scattered and reunite the dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui should be settled at western Turuoqi Spring;[14] Boluomen at Western Sea Commandery. Let each gather his tribes and knit together those who have fled or been torn apart.

sentences.zh: 其爵號及資給所須，唯恩裁處。

translations.literal: Their titles and the supplies required—may Your Majesty's grace alone decide.
translations.idiomatic: Their titles and the provisions they require we leave to Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 彼臣下之官，任其舊俗。

translations.literal: Their subordinate offices—let them follow their old customs.
translations.idiomatic: Let their subordinates keep their own offices and customs.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌所居，既是境外，宜少優遣，以示威刑。

translations.literal: Where Anagui dwells is already beyond the border—it is fitting to send him off with somewhat less favor, to display majesty and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's seat lies beyond the border; his escort should be somewhat restrained, to show the weight of imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 請沃野、懷朔、武川鎮各差二百人，令當鎮軍主監率，給其糧仗，送至前所，仍於彼為其造構，功就聽還。

translations.literal: We request that Woye, Huaishuo, and Wuchuan forts each detach two hundred men, the fort commanders supervising and leading them, supply grain and arms, escort them to the aforesaid places, and there build for them—when the work is done, allow return.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Woye, Huaishuo, and Wuchuan each furnish two hundred men under their garrison commanders, with rations and weapons, to escort the khans to their seats and build their camps; when the work is finished the detachments may return.

sentences.zh: 諸於北來，在婆羅門前投化者，令州鎮上佐準程給糧，送詣懷朔阿那瓌，鎮與使人量給食廪。

translations.literal: All who come from the north and submitted before Boluomen—order the provincial and fort senior aides to supply grain by regulation, send them to Anagui at Huaishuo, and let the fort and envoys measure out rations.
translations.idiomatic: All northerners who submitted before Boluomen did should receive grain by statute from prefecture and fort staffs, be sent on to Anagui at Huaishuo, and be rationed by the fort and his envoys.

sentences.zh: 在京館者任其去留。

translations.literal: Those in the capital hostel—let them go or stay as they choose.
translations.idiomatic: Those lodged in the capital may leave or remain as they wish.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌草創，先無儲積，請給朔州麻子乾飯二千斛，官駝運送。

translations.literal: Anagui is newly establishing his domain and had no stores beforehand—we request two thousand hu of hemp-seed dried grain from Shuozhou, transported by official camels.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui is starting from nothing and has no stores; grant him two thousand hu of hemp-seed provisions from Shuozhou, delivered by imperial camels.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門居於西海，既是境內，資衞不得同之。

translations.literal: Boluomen dwells at the Western Sea—since it is already within the border, supplies and guards cannot be made equal to Anagui's.
translations.idiomatic: Boluomen's seat lies inside our territory at the Western Sea; his escort and supplies cannot match Anagui's.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌等新造藩屏，宜各遣使持節馳驛先詣慰喻，并委經略。

translations.literal: Anagui and the others, newly making a border screen—it is fitting to send envoys each holding credentials by post-haste to comfort and instruct them first, and also entrust overall planning.
translations.idiomatic: As these new frontier lords take up their posts, envoys with credentials should ride ahead to reassure them and oversee the settlement.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Suzong approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔安西將軍、廷尉元洪超兼尚書行臺，詣敦煌安置婆羅門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict ordered Anxi General and Commandant of Justice Yuan Hongchao, also acting as Mobile Secretariat of the Masters of Writing, to go to Dunhuang and settle Boluomen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Emperor Suzong sent Anxi General and Commandant of Justice Yuan Hongchao, with concurrent duties on the mobile secretariat, to Dunhuang to install Boluomen.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門尋與部眾謀叛投嚈噠，嚈噠三妻，皆婆羅門姊妹也。

translations.literal: Before long Boluomen plotted rebellion with his tribesmen to defect to the Hephthalites—the Hephthalite king's three wives were all Boluomen's sisters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Boluomen conspired with his followers to rebel and join the Hephthalites, whose king had taken three of Boluomen's sisters to wife.

sentences.zh: 仍為州軍所討，禽之。

translations.literal: He was then attacked by the provincial army and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops moved against him and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，阿那瓌上表乞粟以為田種，詔給萬石。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year Anagui submitted a memorial begging grain for seed—an edict granted ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year Anagui petitioned for seed grain; the court granted ten thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 四年，阿那瓌眾大飢，入塞寇抄，肅宗詔尚書左丞元孚兼行臺尚書持節喻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Anagui's people suffered great famine; they entered the passes to raid and plunder—Emperor Suzong ordered Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Fu, also acting Mobile Secretariat Master with credentials, to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year famine drove Anagui's people to raid across the border. Emperor Suzong sent Left Assistant Director Yuan Fu, bearing credentials and acting as mobile secretariat chief, to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 孚見阿那瓌，為其所執，以孚自隨，驅掠良口二千，公私驛馬牛羊數十萬北遁，謝孚放還。

translations.literal: When Fu met Anagui he was seized by him; taking Fu along, he drove off two thousand common subjects and several hundred thousand public and private relay horses, cattle, and sheep in flight north, then apologized and released Fu to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Fu met Anagui he was seized and forced to accompany the raid. Anagui carried off two thousand civilians and hundreds of thousands of relay mounts and herds north of the border, then released Fu with an apology.

sentences.zh: 詔驃騎大將軍、尚書令李崇等率騎十萬討之，出塞三千餘里，至瀚海，不及而還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Flying Cavalry General and Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong and others to lead one hundred thousand horse to attack him; they went beyond the passes more than three thousand li to Hanhai and returned without overtaking him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Flying Cavalry General and Minister of the Masters of Writing, was ordered to take one hundred thousand cavalry in pursuit. They rode more than three thousand li beyond the border to Hanhai but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 俟匿伐至洛陽，肅宗臨西堂，引見之。

translations.literal: When Hou Nifa reached Luoyang, Emperor Suzong attended the West Hall and summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Nifa arrived at Luoyang, Emperor Suzong received him in audience at the West Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，婆羅門死於洛南之館，詔贈使持節、鎮西將軍、秦州刺史、廣牧公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Boluomen died at the hostel south of the Luo; an edict posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qin Province, and Duke of Guangmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Boluomen died at the southern hostel in Luoyang; the throne posthumously honored him as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qin Province, and Duke of Guangmu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵反，諸鎮相應。

translations.literal: That year the people of Woye Fort, Poliuhan Baleng, rebelled, and the other forts responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: That year Poliuhan Baleng of Woye Fort rose in revolt, and garrison after garrison followed him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年春，阿那瓌率眾討之，詔遣牒云具仁齎雜物勞賜阿那瓌，阿那瓌拜受詔命，勒眾十萬，從武川鎮西向沃野，頻戰克捷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiaochang, Anagui led his masses to attack them; an edict sent Dieyun Juren bearing miscellaneous goods to comfort and bestow on Anagui—Anagui bowed and received the edict command, mustered one hundred thousand men, and from Wuchuan Fort marched west toward Woye, winning repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xiaochang one (525) Anagui led his warriors against the rebels. Emperor Suzong sent Dieyun Juren with gifts to reward him. Anagui accepted the commission, marshaled one hundred thousand men, marched west from Wuchuan Fort toward Woye, and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 四月，肅宗又遣兼通直散騎常侍、中書舍人馮儁使阿那瓌，宣勞班賜有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Emperor Suzong again sent Acting Direct Drafter of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant Feng Jun as envoy to Anagui, proclaiming comfort and bestowing graded gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Emperor Suzong again dispatched Feng Jun, acting direct drafter of the secretariat and palace attendant, to Anagui with words of comfort and graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌部落既和，士馬稍盛，乃號敕連頭兵豆伐可汗，魏言把攬也。

translations.literal: Anagui's tribes had settled; men and horses grew somewhat strong; he styled himself Khan Chileantou Bingdoufa—in Wei speech, "Grasping."
translations.idiomatic: With his tribes pacified and his strength in men and horses growing, Anagui took the title Chileantou Bingdoufa Khan—"Grasping," in the language of Wei.

sentences.zh: 十月，阿那瓌復遣郁久閭彌娥朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Anagui again sent Yujiulü Mi'e on a tribute mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Anagui sent Yujiulü Mi'e to court again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，阿那瓌遣使人鞏鳳景等朝貢，及還，肅宗詔之曰：「北鎮羣狄，為逆不息，蠕蠕主為國立忠，助加誅討，言念誠心，無忘寢食。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Anagui sent envoys Gong Fengjing and others on tribute; on their return Emperor Suzong addressed them, "The northern garrison tribes rebel incessantly; the Rouran lord has shown loyalty to the state and aided in punishment—thinking on this sincerity, I cannot forget it waking or sleeping."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Anagui sent Gong Fengjing and others with tribute. On their return Emperor Suzong told them: "The northern garrisons seethe with rebellion, yet the Rouran khan has stood loyal to us and helped put the rebels down. When I dwell on such sincerity, it follows me from waking to sleep."

sentences.zh: 今知停在朔垂，與尒朱榮隣接，其嚴勒部曲，勿相暴掠，又近得蠕蠕主啟，更欲為國東討。

translations.literal: "Now I know you halt at the northern frontier, adjoining Erzhu Rong—strictly restrain your followers and do not plunder one another; and I have lately received the Rouran lord's memorial, wishing again to campaign east for the state."
translations.idiomatic: "I understand you are holding the northern marches next to Erzhu Rong. Keep your men under strict discipline and forbid mutual plunder. I have also just received the khan's memorial, offering to march east again in the state's service."

sentences.zh: 但蠕蠕主世居北漠，不宜炎夏，今可且停，聽待後敕。

translations.literal: "But the Rouran lord has dwelt in the northern desert for generations—it is not suited to blazing summer; for now you may halt and await later orders."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the Rouran have always lived in the northern desert and are ill suited to the heat of summer. For the present, hold your forces in place and await further instructions."

sentences.zh: 」蓋朝廷慮其反覆也。

translations.literal: " This was because the court feared his inconstancy.
translations.idiomatic: " The court, in short, feared he might turn treacherous again.

sentences.zh: 此後頻使朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter he frequently sent tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: After that he sent tribute missions again and again.

sentences.zh: 匈奴宇文莫槐，出於遼東塞外，其先南單于遠屬也，世為東部大人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu came from beyond the Liaodong frontier; his forebears were distant kin of the Southern Shanyu, for generations chieftains of the eastern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu came from beyond the Liaodong passes. His line was a distant branch of the Southern Shanyu, and for generations his house had ruled as chiefs of the eastern tribes.

sentences.zh: 其語與鮮卑頗異。

translations.literal: Their speech differed considerably from Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Their language differed markedly from Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 人皆翦髮而留其頂上，以為首飾，長過數寸則截短之。

translations.literal: All men cut their hair but left the crown as head ornament; when it grew past several inches they trimmed it short.
translations.idiomatic: The men all shaved their heads but left the crown bare as an ornament, trimming it whenever it grew more than a few inches long.

sentences.zh: 婦女披長襦及足，而無裳焉。

translations.literal: Women wore long robes reaching the feet, yet had no skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore long robes down to the feet and went without skirts.

sentences.zh: 秋收烏頭為毒藥，以射禽獸。

translations.literal: In autumn they gathered aconite for poison to shoot birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn they gathered aconite to make poison for hunting birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 莫槐虐用其民，為部人所殺，更立其弟普撥為大人。

translations.literal: Mohuai cruelly mistreated his people and was killed by tribesmen; they set up his younger brother Pubo as great chief.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuai abused his people so harshly that his tribesmen killed him and raised his younger brother Pubo as chief.

sentences.zh: 普撥死，子丘不勤立，尚平文女。

translations.literal: Pubo died; his son Qiubuqin succeeded, marrying a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Pubo died his son Qiubuqin succeeded him and took a daughter of Emperor Pingwen to wife.

sentences.zh: [16]丘不勤死，子莫廆立，本名犯太祖諱。

translations.literal: [16] Qiubuqin died; his son Mo'ai succeeded—his original name tabooed the Founding Emperor's name.
translations.idiomatic: [16] When Qiubuqin died his son Mo'ai took the throne; his birth name had violated the taboo on the Founding Emperor's personal name.

sentences.zh: 莫廆遣弟屈雲攻慕容廆，廆擊破之；

translations.literal: Mo'ai sent his younger brother Quyun to attack Murong Hui; Hui defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Mo'ai sent his brother Quyun against Murong Hui, who routed him;

sentences.zh: 又遣別部素延伐慕容廆於棘城，復為慕容廆所破。

translations.literal: He also sent a separate division, Suyan, to attack Murong Hui at Jicheng, and was again broken by Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: he then sent a detached force under Suyan to strike Murong Hui at Jicheng, and was defeated there as well.

sentences.zh: 時莫廆部眾強盛，自稱單于，塞外諸部咸畏憚之。

translations.literal: At this time Mo'ai's tribes were powerful; he styled himself Shanyu, and all outer tribes feared him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mo'ai's following had grown mighty. He proclaimed himself Shanyu, and the tribes beyond the frontier all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 莫廆死，子遜昵延立，率眾攻慕容廆於棘城。

translations.literal: Mo'ai died; his son Xunniyan succeeded and led the host to attack Murong Hui at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo'ai died his son Xunniyan became chief and marched on Murong Hui at Jicheng with a great host.

sentences.zh: 廆子翰先戍於外，遜昵延謂其眾曰：「翰素果勇，必為人患，宜先取之，城不足憂也。

translations.literal: Hui's son Han was first garrisoned outside. Xunniyan told his men, "Han has always been resolute and brave—he will surely become a menace; we ought to take him first—the city is no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Han was posted outside the walls. Xunniyan told his warriors: "Han has always been bold and resolute—he is sure to become a scourge. We should deal with him first; the city itself need not trouble us."

sentences.zh: 」乃分騎數千襲翰。

translations.literal: " He then divided several thousand horsemen to raid Han.
translations.idiomatic: " He detached several thousand horsemen to strike at Han.

sentences.zh: 翰聞之，[17]使人詐為段末波使者，逆謂遜昵延曰：「翰數為吾患，久思除之，今聞來討，甚善，戒嚴相待，宜兼路早赴。

translations.literal: Han heard of it; [17] he sent men posing as envoys of Duan Mobo, going to meet Xunniyan and say, "Han has often been my affliction; I have long wished to remove him. Now I hear you come to attack—excellent. Stand alert and wait; you should take the combined route and come early."
translations.idiomatic: When Han learned of the move, [17] he sent men disguised as envoys of Duan Mobo to meet Xunniyan and say: "Han has long been my bane, and I have wanted him dead for years. Now that you are coming against him, splendid—keep your men ready; take the direct road and hurry to join me."

sentences.zh: 」翰設伏待之，遜昵延以為信然，長驅不備，至於伏所，為翰所虜。

translations.literal: " Han set an ambush to receive him. Xunniyan believed it true, drove hard without precaution; reaching the ambush place he was captured by Han.
translations.idiomatic: " Han laid an ambush. Xunniyan took the story at face value and galloped ahead without precaution until he walked into the trap and was seized.

sentences.zh: [18]翰馳使告廆，乘勝遂進，及晨而至。

translations.literal: [18] Han sent swift messengers to inform Hui; seizing victory he pressed forward and arrived at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: [18] Han sent fast riders to alert Hui, who pressed the advantage and reached the field at dawn.

sentences.zh: 廆亦盡銳應之。

translations.literal: Hui also mustered his elite to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hui himself led out every able fighter to meet him.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延見而方嚴，率眾逆戰，前鋒始交，而翰已入其營，縱火燎之，眾乃大潰，遜昵延單馬奔還，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: Xunniyan saw the array and stiffened; he led the mass to meet battle. As the vanguard just engaged, Han had already entered his camp and set fire to burn it. The host then collapsed in great rout; Xunniyan fled back on a single horse; they captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Xunniyan drew up his ranks and met them head-on. The van had scarcely joined when Han was already inside his camp setting it ablaze. The army broke in panic; Xunniyan fled alone on horseback while the rest were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延父子世雄漠北，又先得玉璽三紐，自言為天所相，每自跨大。

translations.literal: Xunniyan's father and son had been heroes of the northern desert for generations; they had also earlier obtained a jade seal with three toggles, saying Heaven supported them—they always thought highly of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son had lorded over the northern desert for generations and had even come into a jade seal with three cords, claiming Heaven's favor. They had grown insufferably proud.

sentences.zh: 及此敗也，乃卑辭厚幣，遣使朝獻于昭帝，帝嘉之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: With this defeat he used humble words and rich gifts, sent envoys to present tribute to Emperor Zhao; the emperor commended him and gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After this defeat he sent envoys with humble words and lavish gifts to offer tribute to Emperor Zhao. The emperor approved and gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延死，子乞得龜立，復伐慕容廆，廆拒之。

translations.literal: Xunniyan died; his son Qidedui succeeded and again attacked Murong Hui; Hui resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunniyan died his son Qidedui became chief and again marched on Murong Hui, who met him in defense.

sentences.zh: 惠帝三年，乞得龜屯保澆水，固壘不戰，遣其兄悉跋堆襲廆子仁于栢林，仁逆擊，斬悉跋堆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Hui, Qidedui encamped at Baoshui in a fortified camp and would not fight; he sent his elder brother Xibadui to raid Hui's son Ren at Bailin—Ren counterattacked and beheaded Xibadui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Hui, Qidedui fortified himself at Baoshui and refused battle, while sending his brother Xibadui to strike Hui's son Ren at Bailin. Ren counterattacked and killed Xibadui.

sentences.zh: 廆又攻乞得龜克之，乞得龜單騎夜奔，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: Hui again attacked Qidedui and overcame him; Qidedui fled alone by night on horseback; they captured all his followers entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Hui attacked again and broke him. Qidedui fled alone by night on horseback, and his entire following was captured.

sentences.zh: 乘勝長驅，入其國城，收資財億計，徙部民數萬戶以歸。

translations.literal: Pressing victory in a long drive, they entered his capital city, collected wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions, and moved tens of thousands of household tribes back.
translations.idiomatic: Driving the victory home, they entered his capital, seized wealth beyond counting, and moved tens of thousands of tribal households away.

sentences.zh: 先是，海出大龜，枯死於平郭，至是而乞得龜敗。

translations.literal: Earlier the sea had cast up a great turtle that died dried on Pingguo; and now Qidedui was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Years before the sea had cast up a great turtle that died dried out at Pingguo—an omen fulfilled when Qidedui, whose name meant "begging for the turtle," was ruined.

sentences.zh: 別部人逸豆歸殺乞得龜而自立，與慕容晃相攻擊，遣其國相莫渾伐晃，而莫渾荒酒縱獵，為晃所破，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: A man of a separate tribe, Yidougui, killed Qidedui and set himself up; he attacked Murong Huang, sending his state chancellor Mohun to attack Huang—but Mohun indulged in wine and reckless hunting and was broken by Huang; more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui of a cadet line killed Qidedui and made himself chief, then warred with Murong Huang. He sent his chancellor Mohun against Huang, but Mohun gave himself to wine and the chase; Huang shattered him and left more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 建國八年，晃伐逸豆歸，逸豆歸拒之，為晃所敗，殺其驍將涉亦干。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jianguo, Huang campaigned against Yidougui; Yidougui resisted and was defeated by Huang, who killed his fierce general She Yigan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jianguo, Huang campaigned against Yidougui, who resisted and was defeated; Huang slew his champion She Yigan.

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸遠遁漠北，遂奔高麗。

translations.literal: Yidougui fled far to the northern desert and then ran to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui fled deep into the northern desert and finally took refuge in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 晃徙其部眾五千餘落於昌黎，自此散滅矣。

translations.literal: Huang moved his tribal followers, more than five thousand tents, to Changli—from this they scattered and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Huang resettled more than five thousand of their tents in Changli, and from that point the Yuwen power scattered and died away.

sentences.zh: 徒何段就六眷，本出於遼西。

translations.literal: Duan Jiu Liujuan of the Tuohe originally came from Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiu Liujuan of the Tuohe clan came originally from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 其伯祖日陸眷，因亂被賣為漁陽烏丸大庫辱官家奴。

translations.literal: His great-uncle Rilüjuan, because of disorder, was sold as a household slave to the Great Kuru official of the Yuyang Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Rilüjuan, caught up in the turmoil of the age, was sold as a household slave to the chief Kuru officer of the Yuyang Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 諸大人集會幽州，皆持唾壺，唯庫辱官獨無，乃唾日陸眷口中。

translations.literal: The great chiefs assembled at Youzhou, all holding spittoons; only the Kuru official had none—he spat into Rilüjuan's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When the great chiefs met at Youzhou each carried a spittoon; the Kuru officer alone had none, and spat into Rilüjuan's mouth instead.

sentences.zh: 日陸眷因咽之，西向拜天曰：「願使主君之智慧祿相盡移入我腹中。

translations.literal: Rilüjuan swallowed it and, facing west, bowed to Heaven, "May my lord's wisdom, rank, and fortune all shift into my belly."
translations.idiomatic: Rilüjuan swallowed it, faced west, and bowed to Heaven: "May my master's wisdom, rank, and good fortune pass entirely into my belly."

sentences.zh: 」其後漁陽大飢，庫辱官以日陸眷為健，使將之詣遼西逐食，招誘亡叛，遂至強盛。

translations.literal: " Afterward there was great famine in Yuyang; the Kuru official, finding Rilüjuan able, had him lead men to Liaoxi to seek food, recruited fugitives and deserters, and came to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: " Famine later struck Yuyang. Judging Rilüjuan a capable man, the Kuru officer sent him to lead people into Liaoxi in search of pasture, where he gathered fugitives and deserters until his power grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 日陸眷死，弟乞珍代立。

translations.literal: Rilüjuan died; his younger brother Qizhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Rilüjuan died his younger brother Qizhen took his place.

sentences.zh: 乞珍死，子務目塵代立，即就陸眷父也，據有遼西之地，而臣於晉。

translations.literal: Qizhen died; his son Wumuchen succeeded—he was the father of Jiuliujuan—holding Liaoxi lands while acknowledging Jin as overlord.
translations.idiomatic: When Qizhen died his son Wumuchen succeeded—the father of Jiuliujuan—holding Liaoxi while acknowledging the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 其所統三萬餘家，控絃上馬四五萬騎。

translations.literal: He ruled thirty thousand households and more, with forty to fifty thousand horse archers.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled more than thirty thousand households and could field forty or fifty thousand mounted archers.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，幽州刺史王浚以段氏數為己用，[19]深德之，乃表封務目塵為遼西公，假大單于印綬。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mu, Youzhou Inspector Wang Jun, because the Duans had repeatedly served him, [19] was deeply grateful and memorialized to enfeoff Wumuchen as Duke of Liaoxi and grant the great Shanyu seal and cordon.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu, Youzhou inspector Wang Jun, who had often relied on the Duan, [19] repaid them by memorializing to enfeoff Wumuchen as Duke of Liaoxi and invest him with the great Shanyu seal and cordon.

sentences.zh: 浚使務目塵率萬餘騎伐石勒於常山封龍山下，大破之。

translations.literal: Jun had Wumuchen lead more than ten thousand horse to attack Shi Le at Mount Fenglong below Changshan and broke him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Wumuchen with more than ten thousand horsemen to strike Shi Le at Mount Fenglong below Changshan and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 務目塵死，就六眷立。

translations.literal: Wumuchen died; Jiuliujuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wumuchen died, Jiuliujuan became chief.

sentences.zh: 就六眷與弟匹磾、從弟末波等率五萬餘騎圍石勒於襄國。

translations.literal: Jiuliujuan with his younger brother Pidi and cousin Mobo and others led fifty thousand horse to besiege Shi Le at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuliujuan, his brother Pidi, his cousin Mobo, and others led more than fifty thousand horsemen to besiege Shi Le at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒登城望之，見將士皆釋仗寢臥，無警備之意，勒因其懈怠，選募勇徤，穿城突出，直衝末波，生禽之。

translations.literal: Le climbed the wall to watch; he saw officers and soldiers all lay down arms and sleep—no intent of alertness. Le seized on their laxity, selected brave men, broke out through the wall, and charged straight at Mobo, capturing him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Le mounted the wall to look down and saw officers and men had laid aside their weapons and were sleeping with no guard posted. Seizing on their slackness, he picked his bravest men, broke out through the wall, and charged straight at Mobo, taking him alive.

sentences.zh: 置之座上，與飲宴盡歡，約為父子，盟誓而遣之。

translations.literal: He seated him on the bench, drank and feasted to the full, pledged father and son, swore oath and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He seated Mobo beside him, feasted with him to the full, pledged a bond like father and son, and sent him away under oath.

sentences.zh: 末波既得免，就六眷等遂攝軍而還，不復報浚，歸于遼西。

translations.literal: Mobo having escaped, Jiuliujuan and the rest then withdrew the army without reporting to Jun, returning to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mobo was free, Jiuliujuan and the rest withdrew without reporting to Jun and returned to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，末波常不敢南向溲焉，人問其故，末波曰：「吾父在南。

translations.literal: From this onward Mobo often dared not urinate facing south. When people asked the reason, Mobo said, "My father is in the south."
translations.idiomatic: After that Mobo would hardly relieve himself facing south. When people asked why, he said, "My father is in the south."

sentences.zh: 」其感勒不害己也如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his feeling for Le's not harming him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the depth of his gratitude that Le had spared his life.

sentences.zh: 就六眷死，其子幼弱，匹磾與劉琨世子羣奔喪。

translations.literal: Jiuliujuan died; his son was young and weak; Pidi and Liu Kun's heir Qun went to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuliujuan died his heir was still a child. Pidi and Liu Kun's son Qun went to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 匹磾陰卷甲而往，欲殺其從叔羽鱗及末波而奪其國。

translations.literal: Pidi secretly rolled armor and went, intending to kill his paternal uncles Yulin and Mobo and seize the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi marched in secret under arms, intending to kill his uncles Yulin and Mobo and seize the chieftainship.

sentences.zh: 末波等知之，遣軍逆擊，匹磾、劉羣為末波所獲。

translations.literal: Mobo and the rest learned of it, sent troops to intercept; Pidi and Liu Qun were captured by Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo and the others learned of the plot and met him with troops; Pidi and Liu Qun were taken.

sentences.zh: 匹磾走還薊，懼琨禽己，請琨宴會，因執而害之。

translations.literal: Pidi fled back to Ji; fearing Kun would seize him, he invited Kun to a banquet and thereupon seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi fled back to Ji, afraid Liu Kun would arrest him. He invited Kun to a feast and seized and killed him there.

sentences.zh: 匹磾既殺劉琨，與羽鱗、末波自相攻擊，部眾乖離。

translations.literal: Pidi having killed Liu Kun, he and Yulin and Mobo attacked one another; the tribes split apart.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Liu Kun, Pidi warred with Yulin and Mobo in turn, and the tribes fell apart.

sentences.zh: 欲擁其眾徙保上谷，阻軍都之險，以拒末波等。

translations.literal: He wished to lead his masses to relocate and hold Shanggu, blocking the peril of Jundu pass to resist Mobo and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to move his people to Shanggu and hold the Jundu passes against Mobo and the others.

sentences.zh: 平文帝聞之，陰嚴精騎將擊之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu heard of it and secretly mustered elite cavalry to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu heard of it and quietly gathered elite cavalry to strike him.

sentences.zh: 匹磾恐懼，南奔樂陵。

translations.literal: Pidi was afraid and fled south to Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Pidi fled south to Leling.

sentences.zh: 後石勒遣石虎擊段文鴦于樂陵，破之，生擒文鴦。

translations.literal: Later Shi Le sent Shi Hu to strike Duan Wenyang at Leling, broke him, and captured Wenyang alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Le sent Shi Hu against Duan Wenyang at Leling, defeated him, and took Wenyang alive.

sentences.zh: 匹磾遂率其屬及諸塢壁降于石勒。

translations.literal: Pidi then led his followers and all the walled strongholds to submit to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi then led his kin and the fortified hamlets in submission to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 高車，蓋古赤狄之餘種也，初號為狄歷，北方以為勑勒，諸夏以為高車、丁零。

translations.literal: The Gaoche were probably the remnant stock of the ancient Red Di; they were first called Diree; the north called them Chile; the central states called them Gaoche and Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche were likely descendants of the ancient Red Di. They were first known as Diree; northerners called them Chile; the central states knew them as Gaoche or Dingling.

sentences.zh: 其語略與匈奴同而時有小異，或云其先匈奴之甥也。

translations.literal: Their speech was largely the same as the Xiongnu with occasional small differences; some say their forebears were the Xiongnu's sister's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was much like the Xiongnu with minor differences, and some said they sprang from the Xiongnu by a sister's line.

sentences.zh: 其種有狄氏、袁紇氏、[21]斛律氏、解批氏、護骨氏、異奇斤氏。

translations.literal: Their tribes included the Di, Yuanhe, [21] Hulü, Jiepi, Hugu, and Yiqijin clans.
translations.idiomatic: Their clans included the Di, Yuanhe, [21] Hulü, Jiepi, Hugu, and Yiqijin.

sentences.zh: 俗云匈奴單于生二女，姿容甚美，國人皆以為神。

translations.literal: Custom says the Xiongnu Shanyu sired two daughters of surpassing beauty; the people all regarded them as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that a Xiongnu Shanyu fathered two daughters of surpassing beauty whom his people revered as divine.

sentences.zh: 單于曰：「吾有此女，安可配人，將以與天。

translations.literal: The Shanyu said, "I have these daughters—how could I give them to a man? I shall offer them to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyu said, "These daughters of mine cannot be given to any man; I shall offer them to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」乃於國北無人之地，築高臺，置二女其上，曰：「請天自迎之。

translations.literal: " He then in the north of the realm in an uninhabited place built a high terrace, placed the two daughters upon it, saying, "Let Heaven itself come to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: " In an empty tract north of the realm he built a high terrace, set the two daughters upon it, and said, "Let Heaven come to take them."

sentences.zh: 」經三年，其母欲迎之，單于曰：「不可，未徹之間耳。

translations.literal: " After three years their mother wished to welcome them back; the Shanyu said, "Not yet—not until the matter is complete."
translations.idiomatic: " After three years their mother wished to bring them home, but the Shanyu said, "No—not until the rite is finished."

sentences.zh: 」復一年，乃有一老狼晝夜守臺嘷呼，因穿臺下為空穴，經時不去。

translations.literal: " Another year passed, and an old wolf day and night guarded the terrace howling; it bored beneath the terrace a hollow cave and for a long time would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Another year on, an old wolf kept the terrace day and night, howling; it dug a burrow beneath the platform and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 其小女曰：「吾父處我於此，欲以與天，而今狼來，或是神物，天使之然。

translations.literal: The younger daughter said, "Our father placed us here intending to give us to Heaven; now a wolf comes—it may be a divine being; Heaven wills it so."
translations.idiomatic: The younger daughter said, "Father set us here to be given to Heaven. Now a wolf has come—it may be a divine being sent by Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」將下就之。

translations.literal: " She was about to descend to join it.
translations.idiomatic: " She was about to go down to it.

sentences.zh: 其姊大驚曰：「此是畜生，無乃辱父母也！

translations.literal: Her elder sister was greatly alarmed: "This is a beast—will it not shame our parents!"
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister cried out in alarm: "It is only a beast—you will shame our parents!"

sentences.zh: 」妹不從，下為狼妻而產子，後遂滋繁成國，故其人好引聲長歌，又似狼嘷。

translations.literal: " The younger sister did not obey, descended and became the wolf's wife and bore sons; afterward they multiplied into a state—therefore their people love drawn-out song, and it also resembles wolf howling.
translations.idiomatic: " The younger sister would not listen, went down, became the wolf's mate, and bore children. Their line multiplied into a nation, and to this day they love long, drawn-out songs that sound like wolves howling.

sentences.zh: 無都統大帥，當種各有君長，為性粗猛，黨類同心，至於寇難，翕然相依。

translations.literal: They had no commanding great chief; each tribe had its own leader; by nature coarse and fierce, clansmen of one mind—in hardship they cling together.
translations.idiomatic: They had no single paramount chief; each tribe had its own leader. Fierce by nature and clannish, they closed ranks whenever trouble came.

sentences.zh: 鬬無行陳，頭別衝突，乍出乍入，不能堅戰。

translations.literal: In battle they had no formations; each rushed headlong in assault, darting out and in—they could not fight steadily.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they kept no formation, charging in scattered rushes and wheeling back again; they could not stand to a sustained fight.

sentences.zh: 其俗蹲踞褻黷，無所忌避。

translations.literal: Their custom was to squat and behave with coarse liberty, without any scruple.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they squatted familiarly and behaved without restraint or shame.

sentences.zh: 婚姻用牛馬納聘以為榮。

translations.literal: Marriage used cattle and horses as betrothal gifts—this was considered honorable.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage was honored by betrothal gifts of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: [22]結言既定，男黨營車闌馬，令女黨恣取，上馬袒乘出闌，馬主立於闌外，振手驚馬，不墜者即取之，墜則更取，數滿乃止。

translations.literal: [22] Once the agreement was settled, the men's side arranged a corral of wagons and horses and let the women's side take freely; mounting bare-backed they rode out of the corral; the horse owners stood outside the corral, waving hands to startle the horses—whoever did not fall took that horse; if he fell they took another, until the count was full and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Once the match was agreed, the groom's party penned wagons and horses in a corral and let the bride's kin take as they pleased. Each man mounted bareback and rode out; the owners stood outside and startled the horses. Whoever stayed mounted kept the horse; whoever fell had to try again until the allotted number was won.

sentences.zh: 俗無穀，不作酒，迎婦之日，男女相將，持馬酪熟肉節解。

translations.literal: They had no grain by custom, made no wine; on the day of welcoming the bride, men and women went together bearing mare's milk, cooked meat, and joints for feasting.
translations.idiomatic: They ate no grain and brewed no wine. On the wedding day men and women went together carrying mare's milk, cooked meat, and joints of game.

sentences.zh: 主人延賓亦無行位，穹廬前叢坐，飲宴終日，復留其宿。

translations.literal: When the host received guests there was also no seating order; they sat in a cluster before the yurt, feasted all day, and kept them overnight again.
translations.idiomatic: When hosts received guests there was no order of seating; all sat in a heap before the yurt, feasted through the day, and kept them to sleep over again.

sentences.zh: 明日，將婦歸，既而將夫黨還入其家馬羣，極取良馬。

translations.literal: Next day they brought the bride home; then the groom's party went back into her family's herd and took the finest horses to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bride was brought home; then the groom's party rode into her family's herds and took the best horses they could.

sentences.zh: 父母兄弟雖惜，終無言者。

translations.literal: Though father, mother, and brothers regretted it, in the end none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Parents and brothers might grieve, but none would say a word.

sentences.zh: 頗諱取寡婦而優憐之。

translations.literal: They somewhat tabooed taking widows yet treated them with favor and pity.
translations.idiomatic: They were reluctant to take widows, yet treated them with special kindness.

sentences.zh: 其畜產自有記識，雖闌縱在野，終無妄取。

translations.literal: Their livestock had their own marks; though let loose in the wild, in the end none took them wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Each herd bore its owner's marks; even when animals ranged freely in the wild, none were taken by mistake.

sentences.zh: 俗不清潔。

translations.literal: By custom they were not fastidiously clean.
translations.idiomatic: Cleanliness was not a point of custom with them.

sentences.zh: 喜致震霆，每震則叫呼射天而棄之移去。

translations.literal: They dreaded thunder; whenever it thundered they shouted, shot at Heaven, and moved away abandoning the spot.
translations.idiomatic: They feared thunder. Whenever it struck they shouted, shot arrows toward the sky, and abandoned the place to move elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 至來歲秋，馬肥，復相率候於震所，埋羖羊，燃火，拔刀，女巫祝說，似如中國祓除，而羣隊馳馬旋繞，百帀乃止。

translations.literal: When autumn came the next year and horses were fat, they again gathered at the place of the thunder, buried a ram, lit fire, drew knives; the shamaness chanted—somewhat like Chinese purification—and the bands galloped circling, a hundred circuits before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn, when the horses had grown fat, they gathered again at the site of the strike, buried a ram, kindled fire, and drew knives while a shamaness chanted rites rather like Chinese purification. Bands of horsemen galloped in circles a hundred times before stopping.

sentences.zh: 人持一束柳桋，回竪之，以乳酪灌焉。

translations.literal: Each person held a bundle of willow branches, planted them round upright, and poured mare's cheese over them.
translations.idiomatic: Each person carried a bundle of willow wands, set them upright in a ring, and poured cheese over them.

sentences.zh: 婦人以皮裹羊骸，戴之首上，縈屈髮鬢而綴之，有似軒冕。

translations.literal: Women wrapped sheep bones in hide, wore them on the head, coiled and pinned their hair about them—somewhat like a cap and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Women wrapped sheep bones in hide, wore them on their heads, and coiled their hair about them until the effect resembled a court cap.

sentences.zh: 其死亡葬送，掘地作坎，坐屍於中，張臂引弓，佩刀挾矟，無異於生，而露坎不掩。

translations.literal: For death and burial they dug earth into a pit, seated the corpse within, arms spread drawing bow, belt knife and clutching spear—no different from life—and left the pit uncovered.
translations.idiomatic: For the dead they dug a pit, seated the corpse within with arms spread as if drawing a bow, knife at the belt and spear in hand, no different from life, and left the pit open without covering it.

sentences.zh: 時有震死及疫癘，則為之祈福。

translations.literal: When there was death by thunder or epidemic pestilence, they performed blessings for it.
translations.idiomatic: Death by lightning or pestilence called forth blessing rites.

sentences.zh: 若安全無他，則為報賽。

translations.literal: If all was safe without other trouble, they made thank offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When all was well they offered thanks.

sentences.zh: 多殺雜畜，燒骨以燎，走馬遶旋，多者數百帀，男女無小大皆集會，平吉之人則歌舞作樂，死喪之家則悲吟哭泣。

translations.literal: They slaughtered many mixed beasts, burned bone to make flame, galloped horses circling—sometimes hundreds of circuits; men and women, young and old, all assembled; peaceful households then sang and made music; mourning households then mourned in chanted weeping.
translations.idiomatic: They slaughtered many beasts, burned the bones for flame, and galloped horses in circles—sometimes hundreds of rounds. Young and old of both sexes gathered; fortunate households sang and made music, while bereaved families chanted their grief.

sentences.zh: 其遷徙隨水草，衣皮食肉，牛羊畜產盡與蠕蠕同，唯車輪高大，輻數至多。

translations.literal: They migrated following water and grass, wore skins and ate meat; cattle, sheep, and herds matched the Rouran entirely—only their cart wheels were tall and spokes exceedingly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: They moved with the grass and water, dressed in skins and lived on meat; their herds were much like the Rouran's, save that their cart wheels were taller and their spokes far more numerous.

sentences.zh: 後徙於鹿渾海西北百餘里，部落強大，常與蠕蠕為敵，亦每侵盜于國家。

translations.literal: Later they moved to a place more than a hundred li northwest of Luhun Lake; the tribes grew powerful, constantly enemies of the Rouran, and also often raided and plundered our state.
translations.idiomatic: Later they shifted to a site more than a hundred li northwest of Luhun Lake. Their tribes grew strong, were constant foes of the Rouran, and often raided our borders as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖親襲之，大破其諸部。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor personally attacked them and broke their various tribes utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor led a personal campaign against them and shattered their tribes.

sentences.zh: 後太祖復度弱洛水，西行至鹿渾海，停駕簡輕騎，西北行百餘里，襲破之，虜獲生口馬牛羊二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Later the Founding Emperor again crossed the Weak Luo River, marched west to Luhun Lake, halted the carriage and selected light cavalry, went northwest more than a hundred li, raided and broke them, and as captives seized people, horses, cattle, and sheep numbering more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Founding Emperor crossed the Weak Luo again, marched west to Luhun Lake, halted the train and picked out light cavalry, and after riding northwest more than a hundred li struck and shattered the enemy, taking more than two hundred thousand captives together with their horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 復討其餘種於狼山，大破之。

translations.literal: Again he attacked their remaining tribes at Wolf Mountain and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He then pursued their remnant clans to Wolf Mountain and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 車駕巡幸，分命諸將為東西二道，太祖親勒六軍從中道，自駁髯水西北，徇略其部，諸軍同時雲合，破其雜種三十餘落。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage toured; orders were divided among the generals into eastern and western two routes; the Founding Emperor personally led the Six Armies on the center route, from Boyan River northwest raiding their tribes; the armies at one time gathered like clouds and broke more than thirty mixed encampments.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial progress he split his commanders into eastern and western columns while he personally led the Six Armies up the center, sweeping northwest from the Boyan River through their encampments; the columns converged like storm clouds and shattered more than thirty mixed Gaoche bands.

sentences.zh: 衞王儀別督將從西北絕漠千餘里，復破其遺迸七部。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Yi separately supervised generals from the northwest crossing the desert more than a thousand li, again breaking seven scattered fugitive tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Yi, commanding a separate force, crossed more than a thousand li of desert from the northwest and crushed seven fugitive bands that had broken away.

sentences.zh: 於是高車大懼，諸部震駭。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Gaoche were greatly afraid and all tribes were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche were seized with terror, and tribe after tribe trembled.

sentences.zh: 太祖自牛川南引，大校獵，以高車為圍，騎徒遮列，周七百餘里，聚雜獸於其中。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor led south from Niuchuan on a grand battue, using the Gaoche as the enclosure; cavalry and foot soldiers deployed in cordon, circling more than seven hundred li, gathering mixed beasts within.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor led south from Niuchuan on a great hunt, using Gaoche tribesmen as the beaters while horsemen and foot soldiers formed a cordon seven hundred li around, driving every sort of game into the ring.

sentences.zh: 因驅至平城，即以高車眾起鹿苑，南因臺陰，北距長城，東包白登，屬之西山。

translations.literal: Then driving them to Pingcheng, he immediately raised a deer park with Gaoche multitudes, south along the terrace's shade, north facing the Long Wall, east encompassing Baideng, reaching to the western mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The drive ended at Pingcheng, where he set the Gaoche to build a royal deer park bounded on the south by the terrace slope, on the north by the Long Wall, on the east by Baideng, and on the west by the western hills.

sentences.zh: 尋而高車姪利曷莫弗敕力犍率其九百餘落內附，拜敕力犍為揚威將軍，置司馬、參軍，賜穀二萬斛。

translations.literal: Soon after, Gaoche Zhi-li He Mohe Chile Jian led more than nine hundred encampments to submit inward; Chile Jian was appointed General Who Displays Might, with Major and Aide-de-Camp established, and granted twenty thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Gaoche elder Chile Jian of the Zhi-li He clan brought more than nine hundred encampments to submit; he was made General Who Displays Might, given a major and an aide-de-camp, and granted twenty thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 後高車解批莫弗幡豆建復率其部三十餘落內附，亦拜為威遠將軍，置司馬、參軍，賜衣服，歲給廩食。

translations.literal: Later Gaoche Jiepi Mohe Fandou Jian again led more than thirty encampments of his tribe to submit inward; he too was appointed General of Majestic Presence, with Major and Aide-de-Camp, granted clothing, and granted granary provisions yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Gaoche elder Fandou Jian of the Jiepi clan led more than thirty encampments of his people to submit as well; he too received the title General of Majestic Presence, with a major and an aide-de-camp, gifts of clothing, and an annual allowance from the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕社崘破敗之後，收拾部落，轉徙廣漠之北，侵入高車之地。

translations.literal: After the Rouran Shelun's defeat and ruin, he gathered tribes, moved to the far north of the vast desert, and invaded Gaoche territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Shelun of the Rouran was broken in defeat, he gathered what was left of his tribes, shifted to the far northern steppe, and pushed into Gaoche lands.

sentences.zh: 斛律部部帥倍侯利患之，曰：「社崘新集，兵貧馬少，易與耳。

translations.literal: Hulü tribe chief Beihouli was troubled by this, saying, "Shelun is newly gathered, troops poor and horses few—easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli, chief of the Hulü tribe, took alarm and said, "Shelun has only just pulled his people together; his men are few and his horses scant. He will be easy to handle.

sentences.zh: 」乃舉眾掩擊，入其國落。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised his host in a surprise attack and entered their encampments.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his whole force in a surprise strike deep into Shelun's encampments.

sentences.zh: 高車昧利，不顧後患，分其廬室，妻其婦女，安息寢臥不起。

translations.literal: The Gaoche, blinded by profit, disregarded later trouble, divided their lodges, took their women as wives, and rested in sleep without rising.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche, blinded by easy gain, gave no thought to what might follow: they seized Shelun's tents, took his women, and lay down to feast and sleep without a care.

sentences.zh: 社崘登高望見，乃招集亡散得千人，晨掩殺之，走而脫者十二三。

translations.literal: Shelun climbed high and saw; he gathered scattered fugitives obtaining a thousand men, at dawn made a surprise attack and killed them; those who fled and escaped were one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun climbed a height and saw what had happened; he rallied a thousand scattered survivors and at dawn fell on them in a surprise attack. Only one or two in ten of the Gaoche escaped.

sentences.zh: 倍侯利遂來奔，賜爵孟都公。

translations.literal: Beihouli then came fleeing to submit; he was granted the title Duke of Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli then fled to our side and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 倍侯利質直勇徤過人，奮戈陷陳，有異於眾。

translations.literal: Beihouli was straightforward and valiant beyond others, wielding weapons charging into formations, unlike the common lot.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli was blunt, honest, and surpassingly brave; he charged the enemy line with spear in hand in a way unlike ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 北方之人畏嬰兒啼者，[23]語曰「倍侯利來」，便止。

translations.literal: Northerners who feared infants crying, [23] had a saying: when "Beihouli comes," they would stop.
translations.idiomatic: Among northerners who hushed crying infants, [23] the saying ran that once you said "Beihouli is coming," the child would fall silent at once.

sentences.zh: 處女歌謠云：「求良夫，當如倍侯。

translations.literal: Maidens' songs said, "Seeking a good husband, one should be like Beihou.
translations.idiomatic: Maidens sang, "If you want a worthy husband, find one like Beihou.

sentences.zh: 」其服眾如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he commanded the people to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the hold he had over his people.

sentences.zh: 善用五十蓍筮吉凶，每中，故得親幸，賞賜豐厚，命其少子曷堂內侍。

translations.literal: He was skilled at using fifty yarrow stalks to divine fortune and misfortune, and each time hit the mark; therefore he gained intimate favor, rewards thick and generous, and his youngest son Hetang was appointed inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at divining fortune and misfortune with fifty yarrow stalks and was right every time; for this he won the emperor's close favor, received lavish rewards, and had his youngest son Hetang appointed an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 及倍侯利卒，太祖悼惜，葬以國禮，諡曰忠壯王。

translations.literal: When Beihouli died, the Founding Emperor mourned and prized him, buried him with state rites, and gave the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart King.
translations.idiomatic: When Beihouli died, the Founding Emperor grieved for him, buried him with state honors, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart King.

sentences.zh: 後詔將軍伊謂帥二萬騎北襲高車餘種袁紇、烏頻，破之。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered General Yi Yu to command twenty thousand cavalry north to strike the Gaoche remnant tribes Yuan He and Wupin, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict sent General Yi Yu north at the head of twenty thousand horsemen to strike the Gaoche remnant clans Yuan He and Wupin, and he broke them.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，分散諸部，唯高車以類粗獷，不任使役，故得別為部落。

translations.literal: In the Founding Emperor's time, the various tribes were dispersed; only the Gaoche, being by nature rough and uncouth, were unfit for corvée service, and thus were allowed to remain a separate tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Founding Emperor's day the tribes were broken up and resettled; only the Gaoche, deemed too rough and wild for corvée labor, were left as a separate people.

sentences.zh: 後世祖征蠕蠕，破之而還，至漠南，聞高車東部在巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，去官軍千餘里，將遣左僕射安原等討之。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Rouran, broke them and returned; reaching south of the desert, he heard the eastern Gaoche were at Sini Po with very many people and livestock, more than a thousand li from the imperial army; he was about to send Left Deputy Minister Anyuan and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Rouran, routed them, and on his return reached the southern steppe. He learned that eastern Gaoche tribes were camped at Sini Po with vast herds and households, more than a thousand li from his army, and prepared to send Left Deputy Minister Anyuan and others against them.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫翰、尚書令劉潔等諫，世祖不聽，乃遣原等并發新附高車合萬騎，至于巳尼陂，高車諸部望軍而降者數十萬落，獲馬牛羊亦百餘萬，皆徙置漠南千里之地。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Han, Director of the Secretariat Liu Jie and others remonstrated; Emperor Taiwu would not listen, and sent Anyuan and others, also raising newly submitted Gaoche totaling ten thousand cavalry; reaching Sini Po, Gaoche tribes seeing the army surrendered in encampments numbering hundreds of thousands; horses, cattle, and sheep captured also exceeded a million; all were moved and settled on land a thousand li south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Han, Director of the Secretariat Liu Jie, and others urged restraint, but Emperor Taiwu would not hear it. He sent Anyuan with ten thousand horsemen, including newly submitted Gaoche, to Sini Po. Tribe after tribe came over at sight of the army—hundreds of thousands of encampments—and more than a million head of horses, cattle, and sheep were taken. All were resettled within a thousand li south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 乘高車，逐水草，畜牧蕃息，數年之後，漸知粒食，歲致獻貢，由是國家馬及牛羊遂至于賤，氈皮委積。

translations.literal: Riding tall carts, following water and grass, herds multiplied; after several years they gradually learned grain food, yearly presenting tribute; thereby the state's horses and cattle and sheep became so plentiful as to be cheap, felt and hides heaped in piles.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in their tall carts, followed the grass and water, and their herds multiplied. After a few years they began to learn grain cultivation and sent tribute every year. Horses, cattle, and sheep grew so plentiful in the realm that they became cheap, and felt and hides lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，五部高車合聚祭天，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wencheng's time, the five Gaoche divisions jointly gathered to sacrifice to Heaven, the assembly reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng the five Gaoche divisions assembled for a sacrifice to Heaven, and the gathering ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 大會，走馬殺牲，遊遶歌吟忻忻，其俗稱自前世以來無盛於此。

translations.literal: At the great assembly they galloped horses and slaughtered beasts, circling in song merry and joyful; their custom said that since antiquity there had been none more flourishing than this.
translations.idiomatic: At the great gathering they galloped their horses, slaughtered beasts, and circled in song, merry beyond measure; by their own reckoning nothing so grand had been seen since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 會車駕臨幸，莫不忻悅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived on inspection, none was not glad.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came in person, every heart was glad.

sentences.zh: 後高祖召高車之眾隨車駕南討，高車不願南行，遂推袁紇樹者為主，相率北叛，遊踐金陵，都督宇文福追討，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowen summoned the Gaoche multitudes to follow the imperial carriage on the southern campaign; the Gaoche did not wish to go south, and so urged Yuan He Shuzhe as leader, together leading a northern rebellion, roaming across Jinling; Supervisor Yuwen Fu pursued and attacked, was badly beaten and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowen called the Gaoche to follow the imperial train on a southern campaign. Unwilling to march south, they made Yuan He Shuzhe their leader, rose in a mass rebellion, and ranged through the Jinling region. Supervisor Yuwen Fu pursued them and was routed.

sentences.zh: 又詔平北將軍、江陽王繼為都督討之，繼先遣人慰勞樹者。

translations.literal: Also an edict appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Prince of Jiangyang Ji, as supervisor to attack them; Ji first sent men to console Shuzhe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then named General Who Pacifies the North, Prince of Jiangyang Ji, commander of the punitive force. Ji first sent envoys to reassure Shuzhe.

sentences.zh: 樹者入蠕蠕，尋悔，相率而降。

translations.literal: Shuzhe entered the Rouran; soon regretting, together they led surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhe had fled to the Rouran, but soon repented and led his people back in submission.

sentences.zh: 高車之族，又有十二姓：一曰泣伏利氏，二曰吐盧氏，[24]三曰乙旃氏，四曰大連氏，五曰窟賀氏，六曰達薄干氏，七曰阿崘氏，八曰莫允氏，九曰俟分氏，十曰副伏羅氏，十一曰乞袁氏，十二曰右叔沛氏。

translations.literal: Among the Gaoche clans there were also twelve surnames: first Qifuli, second Tulü, [24] third Yizhan, fourth Dalian, fifth Kugu, sixth Dabogan, seventh A'chun, eighth Moyun, ninth Houfen, tenth Fufuluo, eleventh Qiyuan, twelfth Youshupei.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche also reckoned twelve clan names: Qifuli, Tulü, [24] Yizhan, Dalian, Kugu, Dabogan, A'chun, Moyun, Houfen, Fufuluo, Qiyuan, and Youshupei.

sentences.zh: 先是，副伏羅部為蠕蠕所役屬，豆崘之世，蠕蠕亂離，國部分散，副伏羅阿伏至羅與從弟窮奇俱統領高車之眾十餘萬落。
