translations.literal: Earlier, the Fufuluo tribe had been subordinated and enslaved by the Rouran; in Douluon's time the Rouran fell into disorder and the state tribes scattered; Fufuluo's Afuzhiluo with his younger cousin Qiongqi together commanded more than a hundred thousand encampments of Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Fufuluo had been subject to the Rouran. In Douluon's day the Rouran realm fell apart and its tribes scattered; Afuzhiluo of the Fufuluo and his cousin Qiongqi together led more than a hundred thousand Gaoche encampments.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，豆崘犯塞，阿伏至羅等固諫不從，怒，率所部之眾西叛，至前部西北，自立為王，國人號之曰「候婁匐勒」，猶魏言大天子也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe, Douluon raided the frontier; Afuzhiluo and others firmly remonstrated but he would not follow; enraged, they led their following west in rebellion, reaching the northwest of the former Qian tribe, and independently set themselves up as kings; the people called them "Hou Lou Fule," as Wei speech for great Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Taihe, Douluon raided our borders. Afuzhiluo and his men urged him to desist, but he would not listen; in anger they led their people west in revolt, reached the northwest of the former Qian tribe, and set up an independent kingship. Their people hailed Afuzhiluo as Hou Lou Fule—"great Son of Heaven" in Wei parlance.

sentences.zh: 窮奇號「候倍」，猶魏言儲主也。

translations.literal: Qiongqi was titled "Houbei," as Wei speech for stored lord.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongqi took the title Houbei, meaning heir and regent in the language of Wei.

sentences.zh: 二人和穆，分部而立，阿伏至羅居北，窮奇在南。

translations.literal: The two were harmonious, each ruling a division: Afuzhiluo dwelt in the north, Qiongqi in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The two ruled in harmony, each with his own domain: Afuzhiluo in the north and Qiongqi in the south.

sentences.zh: 豆崘追討之，頻為阿伏至羅所敗，乃引眾東徙。

translations.literal: Douluon pursued and attacked them, was repeatedly defeated by Afuzhiluo, and then led his host east in migration.
translations.idiomatic: Douluon pursued them but was beaten again and again by Afuzhiluo and at last led his people east in flight.

sentences.zh: 十四年，阿伏至羅遣商胡越者至京師，以二箭奉貢，云：「蠕蠕為天子之賊，臣諫之不從，遂叛來至此而自豎立。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Afuzhiluo sent merchant Hu Yuezhe to the capital, presenting tribute of two arrows, saying, "The Rouran are thieves against the Son of Heaven; your subject remonstrated and they would not heed, and so rebelled and came here to establish ourselves independently.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Afuzhiluo sent the merchant Hu Yuezhe to the capital with tribute of two arrows and a message: "The Rouran are rebels against the Son of Heaven. I urged them to desist, but they would not listen; I broke away, came west, and set up rule on my own.

sentences.zh: 當為天子討除蠕蠕。

translations.literal: We ought to act for the Son of Heaven in eliminating the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to strike down the Rouran on the Son of Heaven's behalf.

sentences.zh: 」高祖未之信也，遣使者于提往觀虛實。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen did not yet believe him, and sent envoy Yu Ti to observe the truth.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen was not yet convinced and sent the envoy Yu Ti to learn the truth of the matter.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅與窮奇遣使者薄頡隨于提來朝，貢其方物。

translations.literal: Afuzhiluo and Qiongqi sent envoy Bo Nian with Yu Ti to court, presenting their local products.
translations.idiomatic: Afuzhiluo and Qiongqi sent the envoy Bo Nian to court with Yu Ti, bearing local tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔員外散騎侍郎可足渾長生復與于提使高車，各賜繡袴褶一具，雜綵百匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Extraordinary Cadet Attendant Kedu Hun Changsheng again to accompany Yu Ti as envoy to the Gaoche, each granting one suit of embroidered trousers and jacket and a hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Extraordinary Cadet Attendant Kedu Hun Changsheng back with Yu Ti as envoy to the Gaoche, with gifts for each of a brocade jacket and trousers and a hundred bolts of mixed silks.

sentences.zh: 窮奇後為嚈噠所殺，虜其子彌俄突等，其眾分散，或來奔附，或投蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Later Qiongqi was killed by the Hepthalites; they captured his son Mietu and others; his people scattered, some coming to submit in flight, some fleeing to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongqi was later killed by the Hepthalites, who seized his son Mietu and others. His people broke apart, some fleeing to us and some to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 詔遣宣威將軍、羽林監孟威撫納降人，置之高平鎮。

translations.literal: An edict sent Displaying Might General, Feathered Forest Inspector Meng Wei to comfort and settle those who surrendered, placing them at Gaoping Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Displaying Might General and Feathered Forest Inspector Meng Wei to receive the refugees and settle them at Gaoping Garrison.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅長子蒸阿伏至羅餘妻，謀害阿伏至羅，阿伏至羅殺之。

translations.literal: Afuzhiluo's eldest son Zheng Afu married Afuzhiluo's remnant wife, plotted to kill Afuzhiluo, and Afuzhiluo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Afuzhiluo's eldest son Zheng Afu took his father's former wife and plotted to kill him; Afuzhiluo discovered the plot and put his son to death.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅又殘暴，大失眾心，眾共殺之，立其宗人跋利延為主。

translations.literal: Afuzhiluo was again cruel and violent, greatly losing the hearts of the masses; the masses together killed him and established his clansman Baliyan as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Afuzhiluo grew cruel and lost the people's loyalty; they rose together, killed him, and set his kinsman Baliyan on the throne.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，嚈噠伐高車，將納彌俄突，國人殺跋利延，迎彌俄突而立之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the Hepthalites attacked the Gaoche, intending to install Mietu; the people killed Baliyan and welcomed Mietu to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Hepthalites attacked the Gaoche, intending to restore Mietu. The tribesmen killed Baliyan and welcomed Mietu as their king.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突既立，復遣朝貢，又奉表獻金方一、銀方一、金杖二、馬七匹、駝十頭。

translations.literal: Once Mietu was established, he again sent tribute to court, and also submitted a memorial presenting one gold ingot, one silver ingot, two gold staffs, seven horses, and ten camels.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Mietu again sent envoys to court with tribute and a memorial offering one gold ingot, one silver ingot, two gold staffs, seven horses, and ten camels.

sentences.zh: 詔使者慕容坦賜彌俄突雜綵六十匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered envoy Murong Tan to grant Mietu sixty bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the envoy Murong Tan to reward Mietu with sixty bolts of mixed silks.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔之曰：[25]「卿遠據沙外，頻申誠款，覽揖忠志，特所欽嘉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu issued an edict to him, saying, [25] "You hold far dominion beyond the sands and have repeatedly declared loyal intent; reading your steadfast purpose, we especially admire and commend it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu addressed him: [25] "You rule far beyond the desert and have shown your loyalty again and again; your steadfast purpose wins our particular regard."

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕、嚈噠、吐谷渾所以交通者，皆路由高昌，掎角相接。

translations.literal: Rouran, the Hephthalites, and the Tuyuhun have communicated with one another only by routes through Gaochang, linking like pincers.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran, the Hephthalites, and the Tuyuhun have kept in touch only by roads through Gaochang, their positions interlocking like pincers.

sentences.zh: 今高昌內附，遣使迎引，蠕蠕往來路絕，姦勢。

translations.literal: Now Gaochang has submitted within [the realm]; envoys have been sent to welcome and escort [them]. Rouran routes of coming and going are cut off; treacherous designs [—].
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang has now submitted, and we have sent envoys to receive them. The Rouran have lost their lines of travel, and their scheming is checked as well—

sentences.zh: 不得妄令羣小敢有陵犯，擁塞王人，[26]罪在不赦。

translations.literal: you must not rashly allow petty bands to dare offense or obstruction against the Son of Heaven's envoys; [26] the crime is without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: you must not let any petty faction dare to harass or block the Son of Heaven's envoys—[26] that is a crime without pardon."

sentences.zh: 」彌俄突尋與蠕蠕主伏圖戰於蒲類海北，為伏圖所敗，西走三百餘里。

translations.literal: " Soon after, Miedutuo fought the Rouran chief Futtu north of Lake Pulei and was defeated by Futtu, fleeing west more than three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Miedutuo fought the Rouran khan Futtu north of Lake Pulei, was routed, and fled westward more than three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 伏圖次於伊吾北山。

translations.literal: Futtu encamped on the northern hills of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Futtu halted on the northern hills of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 先是，高昌王麴嘉表求內徙，世宗遣孟威迎之，至伊吾，蠕蠕見威軍，怖而遁走。

translations.literal: Earlier, the King of Gaochang Qu Jia had memorialized requesting resettlement within [the realm]; Emperor Xuanwu sent Meng Wei to welcome him. When [Wei] reached Yiwu, the Rouran saw Wei's army and, in terror, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier King Qu Jia of Gaochang had asked to move within the realm; Emperor Xuanwu sent Meng Wei to escort him. At Yiwu the Rouran sighted Wei's troops and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突聞其離駭，追擊大破之，殺伏圖於蒲類海北，割其髮，送於孟威。

translations.literal: Miedutuo, hearing that they had broken camp in alarm, pursued and routed them greatly, killed Futtu north of Lake Pulei, cut off his hair, and sent it to Meng Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Rouran had broken camp in panic, Miedutuo pursued and crushed them, killed Futtu north of Lake Pulei, cut off his hair, and sent it to Meng Wei.

sentences.zh: 又遣使獻龍馬五匹、金銀貂皮及諸方物，詔東城子于亮報之，[27]賜樂器一部，樂工八十人，赤紬十匹，雜綵六十匹。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys presenting five dragon-horses, gold and silver, sable pelts, and various regional goods. An edict ordered Eastern City Attendant Yuliang to respond; [27] he was granted one set of musical instruments, eighty musicians, ten bolts of crimson silk, and sixty bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys again with five dragon-steeds, gold and silver, sable furs, and other tribute. The court ordered Eastern City Attendant Yuliang to reply; [27] the gifts included a full set of instruments, eighty musicians, ten bolts of crimson gauze, and sixty bolts of patterned silk.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突遣其莫何去汾屋引叱賀真貢其方物。

translations.literal: Miedutuo sent his Mohu Qun Fenwuyin Chizi Zhen to present regional goods in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Miedutuo sent his minister Fenwuyin Chizi Zhen of the Mohu office to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，彌俄突與蠕蠕主醜奴戰敗被禽，醜奴繫其兩脚於駑馬之上，頓曳殺之，漆其頭為飲器。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Miedutuo fought the Rouran chief Chunu, was defeated and captured; Chunu bound his two feet to a nag, dragged him to death at a run, and lacquered his skull as a drinking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign Miedutuo fought the Rouran khan Chunu, was defeated and taken alive. Chunu lashed his ankles to a draft horse and had him dragged to death, then lacquered his skull for a cup.

sentences.zh: 其部眾悉入嚈噠。

translations.literal: His tribesmen all entered [the lands of] the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: His people passed entirely under Hephthalite rule.

sentences.zh: 經數年，嚈噠聽彌俄突弟伊匐還國。

translations.literal: After several years the Hephthalites permitted Miedutuo's younger brother Yifu to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later the Hephthalites allowed Miedutuo's brother Yifu to go home and rule.

sentences.zh: 伊匐既復國，遣使奉表，於是詔遣使者谷楷等拜為鎮西將軍、西海郡開國公、高車王。

translations.literal: Once Yifu had restored his state, he sent envoys with a memorial of submission; thereupon an edict dispatched the envoy Gu Kai and others to invest him as General Who Pacifies the West, Duke Who Founded the State of Xihai Commandery, and King of the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu had restored his kingdom he sent a memorial of allegiance; the court dispatched Gu Kai and others to invest him General Who Pacifies the West, founding duke of Xihai, and King of the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 伊匐復大破蠕蠕，蠕蠕主婆羅門走投涼州。

translations.literal: Yifu again routed the Rouran greatly; the Rouran chief Brahmana fled in distress to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu routed the Rouran again; their khan Brahmana fled to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 正光中，伊匐遣使朝貢，因乞朱畫步挽一乘并幔褥，鞦䩛一副，傘扇各一枚，青曲蓋五枚，赤漆扇五枚，鼓角十枚。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era Yifu sent envoys in court tribute and thereby begged one vermilion-painted palanquin with curtains and cushions, one set of hanging screens, one parasol and one fan each, five blue curved canopies, five red-lacquered fans, and ten drums and horns.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengguang he sent tribute and asked for a painted palanquin with curtains and bedding, a set of screen hangings, parasol and fan, five blue curved canopies, five red-lacquered fans, and ten drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 詔給之。

translations.literal: An edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 伊匐後與蠕蠕戰，敗歸，其弟越居殺伊匐自立。

translations.literal: Later Yifu fought the Rouran, was defeated and returned; his younger brother Yueju killed Yifu and established himself [as ruler].
translations.idiomatic: Yifu later fought the Rouran, was beaten, and returned home; his brother Yueju killed him and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 天平中，越居復為蠕蠕所破，伊匐子比適復殺越居而自立。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era Yueju was again broken by the Rouran; Yifu's son Bishi again killed Yueju and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping the Rouran defeated Yueju again; Yifu's son Bishi killed Yueju and made himself king.

sentences.zh: 興和中，比適又為蠕蠕所破。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era Bishi was again broken by the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: During Xinghe the Rouran defeated Bishi once more.

sentences.zh: 越居子去賓自蠕蠕來奔，齊獻武王欲招納遠人，上言封去賓為高車王，拜安北將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Yueju's son Qubin came from the Rouran to submit; Qi Xianwu Wang wished to win over distant peoples and memorialized to enfeoff Qubin as King of the Gaoche, appointing him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yueju's son Qubin fled the Rouran to submit; Prince Xianwu of Qi sought to draw in distant peoples and had Qubin enfeoffed King of the Gaoche, with the titles General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而病死。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖時，有吐突隣部，[28]在女水上，常與解如部相為脣齒，不供職事。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in the time of Taizu, there was the Tuwulin tribe, [28] on the Nüshui River, which regularly with the Jieru tribe were lip and teeth to one another and did not perform tributary duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizu's reign there was the Tuwulin tribe, [28] along the Nüshui, allied with the Jieru like lip and teeth and refusing to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 登國三年，太祖親西征，渡弱洛水，復西行趣其國，至女水上，討解如部落破之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dengguo the Taizu personally campaigned west, crossed the Ruoluo River, again marched west toward their state, reached the Nüshui River, attacked the Jieru tribe, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In Dengguo year three Taizu led a western campaign in person, crossed the Ruoluo, pressed west into their lands, reached the Nüshui, and shattered the Jieru.

sentences.zh: 明年春，盡略徙其部落畜產而還。

translations.literal: The next spring he wholly carried off their tribes, livestock, and goods and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he drove off their people, herds, and goods and returned.

sentences.zh: 又有紇突隣，與紇奚世同部落，而各有大人長帥，擁集種類，常為寇於意辛山。

translations.literal: There were also the Hetulin, of the same tribes in origin as the Hexi, yet each with its own great chiefs and long commanders, gathering clans, who regularly raided about Mount Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Hetulin, kin to the Hexi but under separate chiefs, who mustered their clans and raided around Mount Yixin.

sentences.zh: 登國五年，太祖勒眾親討焉，慕容驎率師來會，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dengguo the Taizu led the masses to attack them in person; Murong Lin led troops to join him and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In Dengguo year five Taizu marched against them in person; Murong Lin brought his army to the rendezvous and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 紇突隣大人屋地鞬、紇奚大人庫寒等皆舉部歸降。

translations.literal: The Hetulin great man Wudijian, the Hexi great man Kuhan, and others all raised their tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hetulin chief Wudijian, Hexi chief Kuhan, and others brought their tribes in submission.

sentences.zh: 皇始二年，車駕伐中山，軍於栢肆，慕容寶夜來攻營，軍人驚走還於國，路由并州，遂反，將攻晉陽，并州刺史元延討平之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangshi the imperial carriage campaigned against Zhongshan and encamped at Baixi; Murong Bao came by night to attack the camp; the troops, startled, fled back to the capital. Their route passed through Bing Province, whereupon they rebelled and were about to attack Jinyang; Bing Province Governor Yuan Yan attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangshi year two the emperor marched on Zhongshan and halted at Baixi. Murong Bao struck the camp by night; the army broke in panic and fled homeward by way of Bing Province, then mutinied and moved on Jinyang. Governor Yuan Yan of Bingzhou defeated and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 紇突隣部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根等復聚黨反於陰館，南安公元順討之不克，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Hetulin tribal commander Ni Wuni, Hexi tribal commander Chinugen, and others again gathered factions and rebelled at Yinguan; Prince of Nan'an Yuan Shun attacked them but could not overcome them; several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Hetulin chief Ni Wuni and Hexi chief Chinugen rallied their factions at Yinguan. Prince Yuan Shun of Nan'an attacked but failed; thousands fell.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，遣安遠將軍庾岳還討匿物尼等，皆殄之。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard of it and dispatched General Who Pacifies the Distance Yu Yue to return and attack Ni Wuni and the others; all were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Yu Yue back against Ni Wuni and his allies and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 又有侯呂隣部，眾萬餘口，常依險畜牧。

translations.literal: There was also the Houluin tribe, more than ten thousand mouths, who regularly pastured relying on rugged terrain.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Houluin tribe, numbering more than ten thousand souls, who pastured in rugged country.

sentences.zh: 登國中，其大人叱伐為寇於苦水河。

translations.literal: During Dengguo its great man Chifa raided as a bandit on the Kushui River.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengguo era their chief Chifa raided along the Kushui.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，太祖大破之，并禽其別帥焉古延等。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year the Taizu routed them greatly and also captured their secondary commander Yanguyan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year eight Taizu crushed them and took their sub-chief Yanguyan and others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 薛干部，常屯聚於三城之間。

translations.literal: The Xuegan tribe regularly gathered and encamped between the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuegan habitually camped among the Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 及滅衞辰後，其部帥太悉伏望軍歸順，太祖撫安之。

translations.literal: After Weichen was destroyed, its tribal commander Taisifu watched the army and submitted; the Taizu comforted and settled him.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Weichen their chief Taisifu came over at sight of the army; Taizu received and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，衞辰子屈丐奔其部。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Weichen's son Qubie fled to his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew, Weichen's son Qubie fled to the Xuegan.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，使使詔太悉伏執送之。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard of it and sent an envoy ordering Taisifu to seize and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent orders that Taisifu seize Qubie and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 太悉伏出屈丐以示使者曰：「今窮而見投，寧與俱亡，何忍送之。

translations.literal: Taisifu brought out Qubie to show the envoy and said, "Now in extremity he has come to trust in us; better to perish together—how could we bear to hand him over?
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu produced Qubie for the envoy and said, "He is ruined and has thrown himself on our mercy; we would rather die with him than betray him to you.

sentences.zh: 」遂不遣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to surrender him.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，車駕親討之。

translations.literal: The Taizu was greatly angered and the imperial carriage personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious and marched against him in person.

sentences.zh: 會太悉伏先出擊曹覆寅，官軍乘虛，遂屠其城，獲太悉伏妻子珍寶，徙其人而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Taisifu had first gone out to attack Cao Fuyin; the imperial army seized the opening, thereupon slaughtered his city, captured Taisifu's wife, children, and treasures, relocated his people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu had marched out against Cao Fuyin; the imperial army struck his empty stronghold, sacked the town, seized his family and treasure, relocated the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太悉伏來赴不及，遂奔姚興，未幾亡歸嶺北。

translations.literal: Taisifu came but could not arrive in time; thereupon he fled to Yao Xing, and before long, ruined, returned north of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu returned too late, fled to Yao Xing, and soon after, a broken man, made his way back north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 上郡以西諸鮮卑、雜胡聞而皆應之。

translations.literal: All the Xianbei and mixed Hu west of Shang Commandery, hearing of it, responded to him alike.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei and other tribes west of Shang Commandery heard the news and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年，屈丐盡劫掠總服之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianci Qubie wholly plundered and brought all under submission.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianci year five Qubie raided until the whole region submitted.

sentences.zh: 及平統萬，薛干種類皆得為編戶矣。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, the Xuegan clans all came to be registered households.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Tongwan the Xuegan were enrolled as regular households.

sentences.zh: 而牽屯山鮮卑別種破多蘭部世傳主部落，[29]至木易干有武力壯勇，[30]劫掠左右，西及金城，東侵安定，數年間諸種患之。

translations.literal: Moreover, a separate branch of the Xianbei of Qiantun Mountain, the Duolan tribe, had from generation to generation held the ruling tribe; [29] when Muyigan came he had martial force and stalwart courage, [30] plundering all about, west to Jincheng and east invading Anding; within several years the various tribes suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: A Xianbei offshoot of Qiantun Mountain, the Duolan, had long held chiefly rank; [29] under Muyigan, a man of force and daring, [30] they raided far and wide—west to Jincheng, east into Anding—and within a few years every tribe around them was in misery.

sentences.zh: 天興四年，遣常山王遵討之於高平，木易干將數千騎棄國遁走，盡徙其人於京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxing [the court] dispatched Prince of Changshan Zun to attack them at Gaoping; Muyigan led several thousand horsemen, abandoned his state, and fled; [Zun] wholly relocated the people to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year four Prince Zun of Changshan was sent against them at Gaoping. Muyigan fled with a few thousand horsemen; their people were moved wholesale to the capital.

sentences.zh: 餘種分迸，其後為赫連屈丐所滅。

translations.literal: The remnant clans scattered; afterward they were destroyed by Helian Qubie.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors scattered and were later wiped out by Helian Qubie.

sentences.zh: 又黜弗、素古延等諸部，富而不恭，天興五年，材官將軍和突率六千騎襲而獲之。

translations.literal: There were also the tribes Chufu, Suguyan, and others, wealthy yet without deference; in the fifth year of Tianxing the Materiel Officer General He Tu led six thousand horsemen in a surprise attack and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes grew rich and insolent; in Tianxing year five Materiel Officer General He Tu led six thousand cavalry in a surprise raid and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 又越勒倍泥部，[31]永興五年，轉牧跋那山西。

translations.literal: There was also the Yuele Beini tribe; [31] in the fifth year of Yongxing they shifted their pastures west of Banashi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuele Beini tribe as well [31] moved their herds west of Banashi Mountain in Yongxing year five.

sentences.zh: 七月，遣奚斤討破之，徙其人而還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month [the court] dispatched Xi Jin to attack and defeat them, relocated their people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xi Jin was sent to defeat them; their people were relocated, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周之獫狁，漢之匈奴，其作害中國固亦久矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Xianyun of Zhou, the Xiongnu of Han—their doing harm to China has indeed been long.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The Xianyun plagued Zhou; the Xiongnu plagued Han—nomads have vexed China for ages.

sentences.zh: 魏晉之世，種族瓜分，去來沙漠之陲，窺擾鄣塞之際，猶皆東胡之餘緒，冒頓之枝葉。

translations.literal: In the Wei and Jin era, tribes were carved apart; coming and going at the desert marches, peering and harassing at the border passes—they were still all trailing threads of the Eastern Hu, branches and leaves of Modu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei and Jin times tribes splintered and shifted along the desert edge, raiding the frontier—yet they were still offshoots of the Eastern Hu, heirs of Modu.

sentences.zh: 至如蠕蠕者，匈奴之裔，根本莫尋，逃刑集醜，自小為大，風馳鳥赴，倐來忽往，代京由之屢駭，戎車所以不寧。

translations.literal: As for the Ruru, heirs of the Xiongnu whose roots cannot be sought, fugitives from punishment gathered into ugliness, growing great from small, wind-swift and bird-hasting, arriving in a flash and departing suddenly—Dai capital was repeatedly alarmed thereby, hence the war chariots knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were Xiongnu stock whose origins could not be traced—outlaws and outcasts who rose from nothing, striking like storm and flock, here one day and gone the next. Dai was shaken again and again; the armies never rested.

sentences.zh: 是故魏氏祖宗揚威曜武，驅其畜產，收其部落，翦之窮髮之野，逐之無人之鄉，豈好肆兵極銳，凶器不戢，蓋亦急病除惡，事不得已而然也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Wei forebears displayed might and flashed martial glory, drove off their livestock, gathered their tribes, cut them down in the wilds at the edge of hair, chased them into lands without people—was it that they loved to unleash weapons to utmost sharpness and would not sheathe cruel arms? Rather, like treating an urgent illness by removing poison—the matter could not be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: So the Wei emperors showed their power, seized their herds and clans, cut them down on the farthest steppe, and drove them into empty country. It was not love of war or refusal to sheathe the sword, but the harsh necessity of rooting out a spreading evil.

sentences.zh: 魏書卷一百三 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，百衲本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校語云：「魏收書列傳第九十一亡。

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 103: in the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked with the character 「闕」(missing); at the end of the Baina, Ji, and Ju editions there is a Song-dynasty collation note stating: 「Wei Shou's Book, Biography 91, is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 103 of the Book of Wei is marked "missing" in the tables of contents of most editions; the Baina, Ji, and Ju copies add a Song note: "Wei Shou's original Biography 91 is lost."

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。

translations.literal: 」The Dian edition's textual verification says: 「Wei Shou's original text is lost; later persons supplemented it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dian edition's notes add: "Wei Shou's text is gone; this is a later supplement."

sentences.zh: 」按此卷以北史卷九八補，唯蠕蠕傳末刪節東、西魏以及齊、周與「蠕蠕」和戰事，遠較北史簡略。

translations.literal: 」According to this, the juan was supplemented from Beishi juan 98, but at the end of the Ruru biography the warfare of Eastern and Western Wei and of Qi and Zhou with the 「Ruru」 was abridged, and is far briefer than the Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: " This juan was restored from Northern History j. 98, but the Rouran account omits Eastern and Western Wei and Qi and Zhou campaigns—far shorter than the Beishi version.

sentences.zh: 依紇突隣部 諸本及北史卷九八蠕蠕傳「紇」作「純」。

translations.literal: Relying on the Hetuolin tribe: in all editions and Beishi juan 98, Ruru biography, 「紇」 is written 「純」.
translations.idiomatic: Hetuolin tribe: various editions and Beishi j. 98 (Rouran biography) read 純 for 紇.

sentences.zh: 按本卷高車傳末即附有紇突隣部，卷二太祖紀登國五年五月及十二月、皇始二年二月見此部，都作「紇突隣」，「純」乃形近而訛，今改正。

translations.literal: According to this, at the end of the Gaoche biography in this juan the Hetuolin tribe is appended; in juan 2, Taizu Annals, fifth year of Dengguo fifth and twelfth months and second year of Huangshi second month this tribe appears, all reading 「紇突隣」; 「純」 is a graphic near-error, and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche section at the end of this juan includes the Hetuolin; Taizu Annals (j. 2) records them in Dengguo year 5 (fifth and twelfth months) and Huangshi year 2 (second month), always as Hetuolin. Chun is a graphic corruption of He; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 狀類於蟲故改其號為蠕蠕 諸本「蟲」作「蠱」，北史卷九八作「虫」，冊府卷九五六

translations.literal: Their appearance resembled worms, so their designation was changed to Ruru; in all editions 「虫」 reads 「蠱」, Beishi juan 98 has the vulgar 「虫」, Cefu juan 956
translations.idiomatic: Because they looked like worms, their name was changed to Ruru; various editions write 蠱 for 虫, the Beishi (j. 98) has the simplified 虫, and the Cefu (j. 956)

sentences.zh: 〈一一二五一頁〉
、通典卷一九六蠕蠕條作「蟲」。

translations.literal: , Tongdian juan 196, Ruru entry, has 「虫」.
translations.idiomatic: ; the Tongdian (j. 196), Rouran section, reads 虫.

sentences.zh: 洪氏考異卷一０以為「蠱」即「蟲」字。

translations.literal: Hong's Kaoyi, juan 10, holds that 「蠱」 is the character 「虫」(worm).
translations.idiomatic: Hong's Textual Variants (j. 10) treats 蠱 as a form of 虫 (worm).

sentences.zh: 按這裏實是字訛，北史作「虫」即俗「蟲」字可證，今據改。

translations.literal: According to this, here it is in fact a character error; the Beishi's 「虫」 proves it is the vulgar form of 「虫」(worm), and it is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: This is a scribal error; the Beishi's 虫 confirms the intended vulgar 虫 (worm character); corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又本傳稱此族「自號柔然」，宋書、南齊書稱「芮芮」，北齊書、隋書作「茹茹」，與「柔然」都是一名的異譯，此譯作「蠕蠕」則是拓跋燾有意侮辱。

translations.literal: Moreover, this biography says this people 「styled themselves Rouran」; the Song Shu and Nan Qi Shu call them 「Ruirui」, the Bei Qi Shu and Sui Shu write 「Ruru」—all variant renderings of one name; rendering them as 「Ruru」(wriggling worms) was Tuoba Tao's deliberate insult.
translations.idiomatic: The biography says they called themselves Rouran; the Song and Southern Qi histories say Ruirui, the Northern Qi and Sui histories Ruru—all the same name in different transliterations. The Wei text's "Ruru" (writhing worms) was Tuoba Tao's deliberate slur.

sentences.zh: 太祖以拔頡為安遠將軍平棘侯 按「拔、頡」指上文之「啟拔、吳頡」，不可能二人同封「平棘侯」，疑「拔」下脫授拔之官爵。

translations.literal: Taizu made Ba and Han Anyuan General and Marquis of Pingji; according to this, 「Ba and Han」 refer above to 「Qiba and Wu Han」—it is impossible for two men to be enfeoffed together as 「Marquis of Pingji」; it is suspected that below 「Ba」 the offices and titles granted to Ba are missing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu enfeoffed Ba and Han as Anyuan General and Marquis of Pingji. "Ba and Han" refer to Qiba and Wu Han above; two men cannot share one marquisate—text likely omits Qiba's title after "Ba."

sentences.zh: 自廣寧還 按卷四上世祖紀神䴥元年八月記拓拔燾「東幸廣寧」，又云「蠕蠕大檀遣子將萬餘騎入塞」，則所謂「自廣寧還」乃指拓跋燾，「自」上當有「帝」字。

translations.literal: Returning from Guangning; according to juan 4, upper, Shizu Annals, eighth month of the first year of Shenlu, it records Tuoba Tao 「eastern progress to Guangning」, and also says 「Ruru Datán sent his son leading more than ten thousand horsemen into the passes」—thus the so-called 「returning from Guangning」 refers to Tuoba Tao; above 「from」 there ought to be the character 「Emperor」.
translations.idiomatic: Returned from Guangning: Shizu Annals (j. 4) records Tuoba Tao's eastern tour to Guangning that year and Rouran Datán's son raiding with ten thousand horse—the subject must be the emperor; Di (emperor) is missing before "returned."

sentences.zh: 樂平王督十五將出西道 通鑑卷一二四

translations.literal: Prince of Yueping supervised fifteen generals out the western route; Zizhi Tongjian juan 124
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yueping led fifteen generals on the western route; Zizhi Tongjian j. 124

sentences.zh: 〈三九０一頁〉
「樂平王」下有「丕」字。

translations.literal: Below 「Prince of Yueping」 there is the character 「Pi」.
translations.idiomatic: After "Prince of Yueping" appears the name Pi.

sentences.zh: 按前後帶兵諸王都具名，不應獨異，當是脫文。

translations.literal: According to this, before and after, princes who led troops all have full names; it should not alone differ—this must be missing text.
translations.idiomatic: Other princes commanding troops are named in full; this lone omission is a lacuna.

sentences.zh: 高涼王那出東道 諸本及北史卷九八「高涼」作「高昌」，通鑑卷一二五

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoliang Na went out the eastern route; in all editions and Beishi juan 98 「Gaoliang」 is written 「Gaochang」, Zizhi Tongjian juan 125
translations.idiomatic: Prince Na of Gaoliang took the eastern route; various editions and Beishi j. 98 read Gaochang for Gaoliang; Zizhi Tongjian j. 125

sentences.zh: 〈三九三六頁〉
作「高涼」。

translations.literal: has 「Gaoliang」.
translations.idiomatic: reads Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 按那附見卷一四高涼王孤傳，襲高涼王爵。

translations.literal: According to this, Na is appended in juan 14, biography of Prince of Gaoliang Gu, and inherited the title Prince of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Na appears in the Gaoliang prince biography (j. 14) and inherited that title.

sentences.zh: 卷七下世祖紀下記歷次重要戰役，幾乎都見高涼王那領兵的紀載，「昌」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Juan 7, lower, Shizu Annals, lower, records successive important campaigns; almost all show Prince of Gaoliang Na leading troops—「Chang」 is a character error, and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu Annals (j. 7, lower) records major campaigns with Prince Na of Gaoliang in command throughout; Chang is erroneous; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 世祖征伐之後 按上敍高宗拓跋濬太安四年事，與此句不貫，「世祖」上疑脫「承」字。

translations.literal: After the Shizu's campaigns; according to this, above narrates Gaozong Tuoba Jun, fourth year of Tai'an—this sentence does not connect; above 「Shizu」 the character 「Cheng」(succeeding) is suspected missing.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu's campaigns: the preceding passage treats Gaozong Tuoba Jun in Tai'an year 4, so the subject breaks—Cheng (successor) likely dropped before Shizu.

sentences.zh: 號伏古敦可汗 冊府卷九九六

translations.literal: Styled Fugudun Khaghan; Cefu juan 996
translations.idiomatic: Took the title Khaghan Fugudun; Cefu j. 996

sentences.zh: 〈一一六九０頁〉

translations.literal: 「Gu」 is written 「Ming」.
translations.idiomatic: reads Ming for Gu.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑卷一三六

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian juan 136
translations.idiomatic: The Zizhi Tongjian (j. 136)

sentences.zh: 〈四二七０頁〉
也作「名」。

translations.literal: also has 「Ming」.
translations.idiomatic: also reads Ming.

sentences.zh: 胡注：「魏收曰『伏名敦，魏言恒也』。

translations.literal: Hu's note: 「Wei Shou says 『Fumingdun, in Wei speech means constant』.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's comment: "Wei Shou says 'Fumingdun means "constant" in Wei language.'"

sentences.zh: 」似司馬光與胡三省所見魏書、北史此傳作「名」，與冊府同。

translations.literal: 」It seems Sima Guang and Hu Sanxing saw the Book of Wei and Beishi in this biography as 「Ming」, the same as the Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Guang and Hu Sanxing's Wei Shu and Beishi copies read Ming here, matching the Cefu.

sentences.zh: 疑「古」字訛。

translations.literal: 「Gu」 is suspected to be a character error.
translations.idiomatic: Gu is likely a corruption of Ming.

sentences.zh: 遣使俟斤尉比建朝貢 諸本及北史卷九八「俟」作「侯」，通志卷二００蠕蠕傳作「俟」。

translations.literal: Dispatched an envoy, Yijin Weibijian, to present tribute at court; in all editions and Beishi juan 98 「俟」 is written 「侯」, Tongzhi juan 200, Ruru biography, has 「俟」.
translations.idiomatic: Sent the envoy Yijin Weibijian to court; various editions and Beishi j. 98 write Hou for Si, but Tongzhi j. 200 (Rouran biography) has Si.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑卷一四八

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian juan 148
translations.idiomatic: The Zizhi Tongjian (j. 148)

sentences.zh: 〈四六三三頁〉
作「俟」，胡注：「俟斤，柔然大臣之名。

translations.literal: has 「俟」; Hu's note: 「Yijin is a Rouran minister's name.
translations.idiomatic: reads Si; Hu notes: "Yijin is a Rouran ministerial title."

sentences.zh: 」下文又見「俟斤丘升頭」。

translations.literal: 」Below again appears 「Yijin Qi Shengtou」.
translations.idiomatic: " Below appears "Yijin Qi Shengtou" as well.

sentences.zh: 「侯」乃「俟」字形訛，今改正。

translations.literal: 「Hou」 is a graphic form-error for 「俟」, and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Hou is a graphic corruption of Si; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 下二年又見同改。

translations.literal: Two years below the same correction appears again.
translations.idiomatic: The same correction applies two years later; not noted again.

sentences.zh: 伏圖納豆崘之妻候呂陵氏 通志卷二００「候」作「俟」。

translations.literal: Futu took as wife Dougun's Lady Hou Lüling; Tongzhi juan 200 「Hou」 is written 「Si」.
translations.idiomatic: Futu married Lady Hou Lüling of Dougun; Tongzhi j. 200 reads Si for Hou.

sentences.zh: 按本卷高車傳附此部，作「侯呂隣」。

translations.literal: According to this, the Gaoche biography in this juan appends this tribe, written 「Hou Lülin」.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche section in this juan appends this tribe as Hou Lülin.

sentences.zh: 考卷一一三官氏志有「叱呂氏，後改為呂氏」。

translations.literal: Examining juan 113, Official Surnames Treatise, there is 「Chilü clan, later changed to Lü clan」.
translations.idiomatic: Official Surnames (j. 113) lists the Chilü clan, later shortened to Lü.

sentences.zh: 元和姓纂卷六、通志氏族略五、古今姓氏書辨證卷二二都作「俟呂鄰」，金石萃編卷二七元宏弔比干墓文碑陰有「俟呂阿倪」。

translations.literal: Yuanhe Xingzuan juan 6, Tongzhi, Clans summary 5, and Gujin Xingshi Shu Bianzheng juan 22 all have 「Si Lülin」; Jinshi Cuibian juan 27, Yuan Hong's eulogy for the Tomb of Prince Bi, stele reverse, has 「Si Lü Ani」.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe Xingzuan (j. 6), Tongzhi Clans (5), and Gujin Surname Studies (j. 22) all write Si Lülin; the Yuan Hong stele to Prince Bi (Jinshi Cuibian j. 27) names Si Lü Ani.

sentences.zh: 「叱」「俟」音近，「候」或「侯」當是「俟」之訛。

translations.literal: 「Chi」 and 「Si」 are close in sound; 「候」(wait) or 「侯」(marquis) ought to be errors for 「俟」.
translations.idiomatic: Chi and Si sound alike; hou (wait) or hou (marquis) are corruptions of si.

sentences.zh: 下高車傳末「侯呂鄰部」同，不再出校記。

translations.literal: At the end of the Gaoche biography below, "the Hou Lülin tribe" is the same; no further collation note is given.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Gaoche biography below, "the Hou Lülin tribe" is treated the same way; no further collation note is given.

sentences.zh: 是以曹道芝北使之日 按上見「曹道」，當是雙名單稱，但「曹道」附見卷七五馮元興傳，他處屢見，並無「芝」字。

translations.literal: "On the day when Cao Daozhi went north as envoy": above we find "Cao Dao"—this should be citation of one half of a double name, but "Cao Dao" appears in the attached biography of Feng Yuanxing in juan 75; elsewhere he appears repeatedly, and nowhere is the character "Zhi" found.
translations.idiomatic: "On the day when Cao Daozhi went north as envoy": the text above reads "Cao Dao," which should be a single-name reference to a double name, but "Cao Dao" appears in the attached biography of Feng Yuanxing in juan 75 and is attested repeatedly elsewhere—nowhere with the character "Zhi."

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌宜置西吐若奚泉 通鑑卷一四九

translations.idiomatic: "Anagui should be stationed at the western Turuo-Xi spring" — Zizhi Tongjian, j. 149

無「西」字。

translations.idiomatic: It lacks the character "west" (西).

sentences.zh: 按上文只稱「吐若奚泉」，疑「西」字衍。

translations.literal: According to the passage above, only "Turuo-Xi spring" is named; "xi" (west) is suspected to be an interpolation.
translations.idiomatic: The passage above names only "Turuo-Xi spring"; "west" (西) is probably an interpolation.

sentences.zh: 未及婚帝入關 此下北史記東、西魏以至周、齊和「蠕蠕」和戰事，於東魏尤詳，本書大加刪節。

translations.literal: "Before the marriage could take place, the emperor entered the Pass": below this, the Beishi records dealings of war and peace between the Eastern and Western Wei through Zhou and Qi and the "Rouran," with particular detail on the Eastern Wei; this book greatly abridges that material.
translations.idiomatic: "Before the marriage could take place, the emperor entered the Pass": from here the Beishi records war and peace with the Rouran through Eastern and Western Wei into Zhou and Qi, with especial detail on the Eastern Wei; this book abridges that material heavily.

sentences.zh: 按北史所述不見他書，其東魏事當即出於魏書。

translations.literal: The Beishi account is not found in other books; its Eastern Wei material must derive from the Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Beishi material is not attested elsewhere; its Eastern Wei passages must come from the Book of Wei.

sentences.zh: 補此傳者刪周、齊時事以就魏書斷限，却連魏書範圍內應有的紀載也一併刪去，殊謬。

translations.literal: Whoever supplemented this biography removed Zhou and Qi matters to fit the Book of Wei's chronological limits, yet also deleted records that should have remained within the Book of Wei's scope—a grave error.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever supplemented this biography cut Zhou and Qi events to match the Book of Wei's chronological frame, yet also removed material that should have stayed within that frame—a serious mistake.

translations.idiomatic: "Married a daughter of Emperor Pingwen": Qian Daxin's Kaoyi, j. 28, says: "Basic Annals

translations.idiomatic: Qiu Buqin married a daughter of Emperor Chuo of Ping, not a daughter of Emperor Yulü of Pingwen—this biography is wrong."

sentences.zh: 翰聞之 諸本脫「翰」字，今據北史卷九八補。

translations.idiomatic: "When Han heard of it": all editions drop "Han"; restored from Beishi, j. 98.

sentences.zh: 為翰所虜 張森楷云：「據此文似遜昵延已見虜矣，而下稱『遜昵延見而方嚴』，兵敗逃還，又與此相矛盾。

translations.literal: "Captured by Han": Zhang Senkai states: "According to this passage, Suniyan would already have been taken captive, yet below it says 'when Suniyan saw him he was stern in bearing,' and after defeat he fled back—this contradicts the present line.
translations.idiomatic: "Captured by Han": Zhang Senkai writes: "This line makes it seem Suniyan was already a prisoner, yet below we read 'when Suniyan saw him he was stern in bearing,' and after defeat he fled back—so the two passages clash.

sentences.zh: 詳玩事勢，此蓋說遜昵延之前驅被虜，非謂遜昵延也，屬文殊欠了晰。

translations.literal: Weighing the course of events, this probably means Suniyan's vanguard was captured, not Suniyan himself—the wording is insufficiently clear."
translations.idiomatic: On the merits of the narrative, this probably refers to Suniyan's vanguard being taken, not Suniyan himself—the text is not clear enough."

sentences.zh: 」按通志卷二００宇文莫槐傳「虜」作「敗」，當是以意改。

translations.idiomatic: In the Yuwen Mohuai biography in Tongzhi, j. 200, "captured" reads "defeated"—probably an editorial change.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時幽州刺史王浚以段氏數為己用 百衲、南、汲、局四本「穆帝」上有「晉」字，又無「時」字，北本、殿本及北史卷九八如上摘句。

translations.literal: "In the time of Emperor Mu, Wang Jun, governor of You Province, repeatedly employed the Duan clan": the Baibai, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions place "Jin" before "Emperor Mu" and omit "time"; the Bei and Dian editions and Beishi, juan 98, read as quoted above.
translations.idiomatic: "In the time of Emperor Mu, Wang Jun of You Province repeatedly used the Duan clan": the Baibai, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions add "Jin" before "Emperor Mu" and drop "time"; the Bei and Dian editions and Beishi, j. 98, agree with the quotation above.

sentences.zh: 按此穆帝指拓跋猗盧，補此傳者妄加「晉」字，又刪「時」字，遂使死於西晉之王浚忽為三十餘年後東晉穆帝的幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Here "Emperor Mu" means Tuoba Yilu; whoever supplemented this biography wrongly added "Jin" and deleted "time," so that Wang Jun, who died in Western Jin, suddenly becomes governor of You under Eastern Jin's Emperor Mu more than thirty years later.
translations.idiomatic: Here "Emperor Mu" is Tuoba Yilu. Whoever supplemented this biography added "Jin" and cut "time," turning Wang Jun—dead in Western Jin—into a You governor under Eastern Jin's Emperor Mu thirty years later.

sentences.zh: 北、殿本據北史改是，今從之。

translations.literal: The Bei and Dian editions, emended according to the Beishi, are correct; the text follows them here.
translations.idiomatic: The Bei and Dian editions, corrected from the Beishi, are right; we follow them here.

sentences.zh: 國人立日陸眷弟護遼為主 按日陸眷是末波祖父輩，其弟亦是從祖，似不能嗣末波位。

translations.literal: "The tribesmen installed Hulu, younger brother of Rilujuan, as ruler": Rilujuan was of Mobo's grandfather's generation, and his younger brother would also be a great-uncle—it seems he could not succeed to Mobo's position.
translations.idiomatic: "The tribesmen installed Hulu, Rilujuan's younger brother, as ruler": Rilujuan belonged to Mobo's grandfather's generation; a younger brother would be a great-uncle and could hardly succeed Mobo.

sentences.zh: 晉書卷六三段匹磾傳稱末波死，弟牙立，牙死，其後從祖就陸眷之孫遼

translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu, j. 63, biography of Duan Pidi, says that when Mobo died his younger brother Ya took the throne; when Ya died, the great-uncle Jiulujuan's grandson Liao

translations.idiomatic: "Yuanhe clan": all editions and Beishi, j. 98, write 袁 as 表; Imperial Readings, j. 801

translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe is the Weihe of the Tiele account in Sui Shu, j. 84—the Uyghurs of Tang times.

translations.idiomatic: 表 is a graphic corruption of 袁; emended here from the Imperial Readings.

translations.idiomatic: "Northerners fear those who make infants cry" — Beishi, j. 98; Imperial Readings, j. 801

「畏」下有「之」字，疑當有此字。

translations.idiomatic: After 畏 there is 之 ("them"); the particle probably belongs in the text.

translations.idiomatic: "Second, the Tulü clan": Tongdian, j. 197, and the Gaoche account in Tongzhi, j. 200, write 吐 as 叱.

translations.idiomatic: Below the text has "Shizong"; 祖 is a corruption and is emended here.

translations.literal: Beishi, juan 98, reads "Yu"; the Dian edition presumably emended accordingly from the Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi, j. 98, has 于; the Dian edition likely followed it.

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from the Beishi; the Dian edition is followed here.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter was restored from the Beishi; we follow the Dian edition.

translations.literal: "There was the Tutulin tribe": in Taizu Annals, juan 2, Dengguo year 2, fourth month, day Guiji, and in the biography of Wei Guzhen, juan 26, "Tu" (吐) is written "Chi" (叱) throughout—"Tu" is suspected to be corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: "The Tutulin tribe": in j. 2 (Dengguo 2, month 4, day Guiji) and j. 26 (Wei Guzhen) the graph is 叱 not 吐; 吐 is probably corrupt.

translations.idiomatic: "Qiantun Mountain Xianbei, Poduolan chieftain line": all editions read 牽 as 率; Beishi, j. 98, has 帥.

sentences.zh: 按卷七五尒朱天光傳稱万俟道洛「率眾西依牽屯山」，周書卷一文帝紀、卷一０邵惠公顥附宇文導傳稱導追斬侯莫陳悅於「牽屯山」。

translations.literal: Biography of Erzhu Tianguang, juan 75, says Wanqidao Luo "led his masses west to rely on Qiantun Mountain"; Zhou Shu, juan 1, Wendi Annals, and the appended biography of Yuwen Dao in Shaohui Gong Hao, juan 10, say Dao pursued and beheaded Houmochen Yue at "Qiantun Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: J. 75 (Erzhu Tianguang) has Wanqidao Luo settling at Qiantun Mountain; Zhou Shu, j. 1 and j. 10 (Yuwen Dao), place Houmochen Yue's death at Qiantun Mountain.

translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing cites Du You: "Qiantun Mountain lies in Gaoping County, Yuanzhou
